The same induced prompt improves mean judge scores across seven Generators by 7.1-19.2 percentage points, including an increase from 85.3% to 97.5% for the induction model. A separate compression study reduces prompt length by 52.7% with a 0.19-percentage-point score decrease. An assistant using the induced prompt is in early access, with initial user feedback to inform subsequent refinement.

title: Linear resolutions of powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs with matching number four
abstract: For a finite simple gap-free graph $G$, let $B(G)$ denote the vertices $v$ for which $G-N_G[v]$ is not co-chordal, and put $C(G)=V(G)\setminus B(G)$. We prove a sufficient condition for all ordinary powers of its edge ideal to have linear resolutions from the second power onward: every induced anticycle of length at least five must contain an edge with both endpoints in $C(G)$. The argument uses variable generators of augmented colon ideals to eliminate anticycles that may persist in the ordinary quadratic colons. It yields linear resolutions for all powers $I(G)^q$, $q\ge2$, whenever the ordinary matching number is at most four, which answers the first part of a question of Erey, Hà, Hibi, Kara and Morey. The criterion also applies to certain graphs with adjacent exceptional vertices and matching number five. The proofs are theoretical and valid over arbitrary fields. We do not assert linear quotients.

title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.

title: 4K Image Super-Resolution on Mobile NPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
abstract: Image super-resolution is widely used on mobile devices for upscaling various types of image data. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on neural processing units (NPUs) present in the majority of mobile and IoT chipsets. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can upsample images from Full HD to 4K resolution while running on popular mobile NPUs from Qualcomm and MediaTek. For this, the participants were provided with the DIV2K dataset and trained models to do an efficient 3X image upscaling. The competition had two tracks: in the first track, the models had to be fully quantized (INT8), and the runtime of all models was evaluated on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 NPU. In the second track, the participants were developing floating-point solutions that were evaluated on the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 NPU. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to reconstruct 4K images under 5 milliseconds while reaching a PSNR score of 30 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.

title: High-Frequency Estimation of the Leverage Effect under Rough Volatility with Microstructure Noise
abstract: This paper develops feasible high-frequency inference for the leverage effect when the spot variance follows rough Volterra dynamics, leverage loadings depend on endogenous rough states, and observed prices may be contaminated by microstructure noise. We define an integrated leverage parameter through a scaled covariation between log prices and spot variance that accounts for their different local fluctuation scales. The scaled realized covariation admits a stable functional central limit theorem with an explicit pathwise centering correction arising from within-interval variation in the leverage loading. A loading regularity condition renders this correction asymptotically negligible, and we verify the condition for direct Volterra loadings and for smooth functions of closed rough states for every Hurst index below one half. We construct a block-based estimator with an exact finite-window correction for the leading proportional bias, together with a nonnegative single-scale estimator of its asymptotic variance. Pre-averaging extends feasible inference to observations with independent and identically distributed microstructure noise. Simulations under the rough Heston model demonstrate accurate finite-sample calibration with and without noise. An empirical application to fifteen years of one-second data on nine U.S. equities and ETFs finds negative median leverage estimates for every asset at weekly and monthly horizons.

title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

title: RTP-LLM: Building an Evolvable and Reliable LLM Inference Engine at Alibaba Scale
abstract: Large language models and inference techniques evolve rapidly, making model enablement a recurring production task rather than a one-time integration effort. At Alibaba, a shared inference infrastructure must keep pace with new models and serving capabilities while remaining reliable across heterogeneous production environments. To reconcile rapid evolution with production reliability, we present RTP-LLM, an open-source production inference engine developed and deployed at Alibaba. Its architecture separates model-specific execution from shared request processing, state management, and resource coordination. Explicit interfaces localize compatible model changes while allowing models and deployment configurations to reuse common serving mechanisms. RTP-LLM has evolved from an exploratory system into a shared production engine that supports $\sim$100 models and processes hundreds of trillions of tokens per day. We describe how its architecture and production practices accommodate model evolution and contain the impact of failures, and share lessons for building evolvable and reliable inference engines at enterprise scale.

title: Autotuning GPU Thread Block Sizes for Large-Scale Stencil Applications Using the OPS DSL
abstract: Large-scale structured-mesh stencil applications can run for hours or days on modern HPC GPU platforms, making launch-configuration choices important. OPS enables high-level stencil codes to target multiple GPU architectures, but its GPU backends rely on a default or user-selected global block/workgroup shape, even though different kernels, problem geometries, and architectures may favor different configurations. This paper presents a transparent per-kernel block/workgroup-shape autotuning extension for OPS. The extension explores valid block/workgroup shapes during execution, records the fastest configuration for each kernel, and enables precomputed replay of the selected configurations in subsequent runs. We evaluate the approach on structured-mesh proxy and academic research applications, covering 459 unique kernels across 3 NVIDIA and 2 AMD GPUs. The evaluation reports speedup distributions, representative wall-time summaries, timing variability, and input problem shape effects. Replaying the best per-kernel launch shapes improves 923 of 995 measured application/input/GPU cases over the default OPS shape. Depending on the GPU, the median speedup ranges from 1.02x to 1.18x, with individual configurations of LAPL2D, TTI3D, and OpenSBLI-based TGV solvers exceeding 1.5x. The results also show that performance sensitivity is not limited to launch shape. At fixed cell count, changing the input problem shape changes precomputed-replay runtime by 0.8-34.6% in representative cases, while kernel-level timing variability depends on the interaction between runtime contribution, input problem shape, and GPU/backend behavior. Overall, automatic per-kernel block/workgroup-shape selection improves OPS performance across GPUs, provided shape sensitivity and timing stability are interpreted together.

title: Decay Rate toward the Rarefaction Wave and the Viscous Contact Wave for Jin--Xin Relaxation Model
abstract: This paper establishes the time-decay rates toward the rarefaction wave and the viscous contact wave for the one-dimensional Jin--Xin relaxation system under the $L^1$ integrability condition of the initial perturbation. In the case of a strictly convex flux, we employ a decomposition method to derive a logarithmic $L^1$ estimate related to a conjecture proposed by Liu\cite{liu2001lp}. Furthermore, a time-weighted $L^2$ method yields the optimal decay rate toward the rarefaction wave. Regarding the case where the flux is partially linearly degenerate, by employing a similar \(L^1\) estimate and time-weighted \(L^2\) method, along with a refined estimate of the nonlinear wave interactions, we obtain the corresponding decay rate toward the composite wave. The decay estimates are obtained without smallness assumptions on the initial perturbations or the wave strength.

title: A JWST/NIRSpec Catalog of Low-Mass Candidates toward NGC 2024 from Multi-component Spectral Modeling
abstract: Young low-mass objects in crowded, highly obscured star-forming regions are difficult to characterize. Deriving reliable physical parameters requires separating photospheric emission from complex extinction and circumstellar emission. We apply a multi-component spectral-modeling framework to JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra toward NGC 2024, obtaining adopted fits for 78 sources. The framework incorporates atmospheric models, dust and ice opacities, and optional thermal emission. Most spectra favor additional large-H$_2$O-ice opacity over the baseline small-grain model, while a smaller subset requires additional gray opacity, potentially arising from large refractory grains. Some spectra also require a thermal component to reproduce the long-wavelength continuum. The parameters inferred with this framework, together with the NGC 2024 distance, yield radii and bolometric luminosities. Comparison with evolutionary models for young low-mass and substellar objects provides mass estimates and identifies 46 candidate members, 27 sources classified as background, and five uncertain sources. Candidate members show lower fitted surface gravities than likely background stars. Of the candidate members, 23 lie above the youngest available isochrones, plausibly reflecting the cluster's youth and uncertainties in model initial conditions. The resulting catalog provides a uniform characterization of the NGC 2024 sample and establishes a framework for treating complex extinction and circumstellar emission in JWST spectra of other obscured star-forming regions.

title: E-UDE: A Scientific Machine Learning Model for Malware Propagation Dynamics
abstract: Understanding the malware propagation dynamics over the Internet is crucial for effectively controlling its spread. Existing mechanistic and data-driven models in the context of malware propagation dynamics, have some issues with either interpretability or predictive accuracy. This study presents an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework that explicitly incorporates more detailed key factors that influence malware propagation. Evaluation on real-world malware propagation data shows that the E-UDE achieves the best overall performance, attaining an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65. Compared with the Classical ODE and the UDE models, the proposed approach reduces RMSE by approximately 66 percent and 39 percent, respectively. Its robustness to predictive capability is further evaluated. In this experiment, the E-UDE achieves a Test RMSE of 634.6, a Test MAE of 419.3, and a Test Correlation of 0.964. The E-UDE maintains relatively stable prediction performance as the noise level increases, showing limited degradation compared with the baseline models. Furthermore, this E-UDE model enables us to perform several scenario analyses under different cybersecurity scenarios, providing a useful framework for better understanding the effective control factors. To study the wide applicability of the E-UDE framework, the model performance is assessed by two different datasets, namely, Code Red dataset and Witty Worm dataset.

title: PACT: Defending Recommendation against Promotional News Rewriting via Attack-Diverse Score Consistency
abstract: Personalized news recommenders are increasingly vulnerable to LLM-powered promotional attacks, where content providers rephrase headlines to manipulate rankings without altering underlying facts. Defending against such manipulation requires covering a wide spectrum of LLM generators and optimization strategies--ranging from stylistic prompting to reinforcement feedback--without incurring prohibitive training or inference costs. In this work, we present PACT (Pooled Attack Consistency Training), a model-agnostic defense that decouples relevance estimation from superficial rhetorical variations. PACT integrates three synergistic operations: it pools offline, fact-checked rewrites from multi-generator and multi-strategy attack sources; samples a constant number of variants at each training visit to yield an unbiased estimator of the pool-wide consistency objective under a fixed compute budget; and aligns original and rewritten ranking scores within the same user context jointly with click supervision. Requiring no architectural modifications or test-time filtering, PACT deploys the trained recommender with zero extra latency. Across nine experimental settings spanning three recommendation backbones and three unseen-generator attacks, PACT consistently achieves the lowest promotion rate and target exposure, outperforming the strongest defense baseline by up to 3.0 percentage points in promotion reduction under LANCE. Further evaluations verify that PACT's superiority holds robustly under unseen attack-strategy holdouts and adaptive white-box retraining, while keeping clean recommendation utility virtually intact.

title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
abstract: Let $φ=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The set $\{0,φ,φ^2,φ^3\}$ is classical (Euclid, Elements XIII.8): by $φ^2=φ+1$ its six pairwise differences take the values $1,φ,φ^2,φ^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write it as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, $a=φu$, $b=φ^2u$, $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. No five distinct reals have all their positive differences in $\{uφ^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$; this follows from a result of Lenstra (1977), and we give a self-contained proof. We give an elementary proof of uniqueness: every four-element set with this property is a translate of $uφ^m\{0,φ,φ^2,φ^3\}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$, and if all its differences lie in $\{u,φu,φ^2u,φ^3u\}$ it is a translate of $S$. Among all $x>1$, only $x=φ$ admits a four-point set of reals whose set of distinct differences is $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$. For the analogous quadruple with base $x\neqφ$ the failure is measured by two closure residues, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^2$ and $\pm \mathrm{Fib}_{n+1}u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^3$. The cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2πd t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(πa t)\cos^2(πb t)-2$; it is not periodic but is Bohr almost periodic, with explicit almost periods $τ_n=\mathrm{Fib}_n/u$, and we determine the two-term asymptotics $\sup_t|C_S(t+τ_n)-C_S(t)|=6\sqrt3 πφ^{-n}-2\sqrt3 π^3φ^{-3n}+O(φ^{-5n})$, with optimal constants; the inclusion length of the $\varepsilon$-almost periods is of order $1/\varepsilon$. For a scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $ν_n=Kφ^{-n}$ realises the construction with differences $ν_{200},\dots,ν_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. All proofs are elementary and self-contained.

title: Efficient Image Denoising on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
abstract: Image denoising is a fundamental problem in mobile photography. Despite a large number of solutions proposed for this task, the majority of them are trained on synthetically produced noisy images, and are additionally too computationally heavy for processing full-resolution images on mobile devices. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can denoise Full HD resolution photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale dataset consisting of noisy-clean image pairs captured in the wild. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to perform high-quality image denoising under 100 milliseconds on both platforms while reaching a PSNR score of over 37 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $μ_n \to μ$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.

title: Curvature pinching for minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in spheres
abstract: We prove a rigidity theorem for closed connected minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in the unit sphere. In every dimension $n\geqslant 3$, such a hypersurface is totally geodesic if the squared norm of its Riemannian curvature tensor is at most $2n(n-1)$.

title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
abstract: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.

title: Generalizable robotic manipulation through compositional skill reuse
abstract: Hao Ren, Shuohan Chen, Senyuan Mu, Ruihan Huang, Wanfeng Shang, Yajing Shen

title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
abstract: Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem. We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.

title: Probing Hidden Dimensions with Multimessenger Gravitational Waves
abstract: The dimensionality of spacetime is a fundamental property of nature, yet whether our observed four-dimensional spacetime is embedded in a higher-dimensional geometry remains experimentally unresolved. Gravitational waves (GWs) offer a direct probe of compact extra dimensions through the strong-field dynamics of binary coalescences. In this work, we investigate extra-dimensional modifications to GW generation within a compactified Kaluza--Klein framework. We derive the Newtonian conservative binary dynamics and the leading-order extra-dimensional correction to the GW energy flux and formulate the corresponding waveform modifications within the parameterized post-Einsteinian (ppE) framework. Combining these results with the previously derived 1PN amplitude correction arising from perturbations of the internal volume, we construct modified GW waveform templates for ground- and space-based detectors. To alleviate parameter degeneracies in GW parameter estimation, we combine the observed strain data of GW170817 with independent electromagnetic observations in a multimessenger Bayesian analysis, yielding a 95\% credible upper bound of $n<0.11$ on the phenomenological dimensional parameter. We further investigate injected multimessenger massive black hole binary observations with Taiji, finding that the upper bound could be improved by nearly two orders of magnitude to $n<0.00178$. These results highlight the potential of multimessenger GW observations to probe extra-dimensional effects and test fundamental gravity in the strong-field and dynamical regime.

title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the resulting average within the indifferent class. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.

title: Locally Conformal Analysis of Non-Degenerate Odd Pairs
abstract: We study the locally conformal geometry of cosymplectic and coorientable contact manifolds within a common algebraic framework based on a non-degenerate odd pair: a one-form and a two-form whose appropriate wedge product defines a nowhere-vanishing top-degree form on an odd-dimensional manifold. We consider conformally compatible local geometric and Hamiltonian data and encode their gluing through a closed Lee form and the Lichnerowicz-de Rham differential. For locally conformal cosymplectic geometry, we introduce an equal-weight formulation in which the defining forms carry the same conformal weight. This formulation allows compatible local Hamiltonian vector fields to glue directly into a global Hamiltonian vector field without additional rescaling, thereby preserving the local dynamics. For contact geometry, we develop a twisted odd-pair formulation in which the Lee form records the conformal gluing of local Hamiltonian data, while the global one-form remains an ordinary contact form. We illustrate these constructions through time-dependent mass dynamics in the cosymplectic setting and dissipative particle dynamics in the contact setting.

title: A Token Is Not a Unit of Difficulty: Segmentation Controls Where Adaptive Computation Goes Inside a Word
abstract: Early-exit language models decide for each token how much computation to spend, usually by stopping once the prediction is confident. Yet a token is not a fixed unit: tokenizers cut words into different numbers of pieces in different languages. We ask where inside a word such a policy spends its budget. In Qwen3, along two adaptive axes (the timesteps of a spiking conversion and the layers of the original Transformer), confidence stopping gives the continuation pieces of a word less computation than its first piece in English, German, and Turkish, but more in Bangla. Segmentation drives this. Re-segmenting the same parallel passages with BPE-dropout shifts the gap by up to eight exits on both axes, small models trained under two tokenizers shift Bangla's gap by six exits, and BLOOM and mGPT, which split Bangla less finely, give it the English pattern. Characters per token do not predict the gap across languages; within-word surprisal explains 75% of its variance. A learned stopping head beats confidence stopping by 7 to 8 points, but gains less than one point over the best mix of fixed exits at equal cost, and sometimes loses. All results come from offline analysis, not measured speedups.

title: Common-Source Assembly for Spherical Minimal Immersions
abstract: We develop a matching principle for assembling maps from a common manifold into spherical minimal immersions. The equations couple the coefficients to the induced metric and yield examples with nonminimal constituent immersions. We establish existence and uniqueness of matching coefficients under suitable hypotheses and sharp rigidity for complete harmonic assemblies over $\mathbb S^2$. For a Clifford family, the first eigenspace determines the underlying fibration. The principle also produces weighted minimal profiles that generate minimal products in round spheres, with examples formed from finitely many Lawson--Osserman blocks of different degrees over a common Hopf source.

title: Normal Factor Graph Representations of Stabilizer Quantum Codes with Applications
abstract: We develop normal factor graph (NFG) representations of stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes and entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes. We introduce two complementary representations. Quantum-code NFGs describe stabilizer and normalizer label codes and provide a graphical framework for establishing self-orthogonality, constructing codes from component codes, and identifying encoding and decoding circuits. Quantum-probability NFGs represent the quantum-mechanical probabilities associated with encoding, noise, and measurement. We also introduce a doubleedge formulation that makes the relationship between these two representations explicit. We apply the framework to convolutional and tail-biting convolutional stabilizer codes, as well as to two classes of low-density parity-check stabilizer codes. Finally, we extend the quantum-probability representation to entanglementassisted codes.

title: HALO: Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records
abstract: Learning from extensive longitudinal clinical records--spanning repeated encounters, evolving conditions, and heterogeneous documentation--under a finite labeling budget requires solving two coupled problems: deciding what evidence to keep and deciding which patients deserve higher-fidelity labels. Prior work on active learning and multi-fidelity label acquisition mainly addresses the second problem, while treating the evidence presented to the acquisition policy as fixed. We present HALO, a Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning pipeline for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records. This framework jointly learns what to read and what label source to acquire under budget. HALO first selects informative evidence from longitudinal records and then uses a budget-aware policy to allocate free-, silver-, and gold-fidelity label sources. For frozen policies, our theory characterizes asymmetric acquired-label channels and gives a budget-constrained finite-sample gold-risk bound for a common downstream logistic model. In a heart-failure case study, HALO attained the highest MedAlign acquired-label F1 at six of eight target budgets. A downstream classifier trained on HALO-acquired labels attained the highest external MGB F1 at budgets 15-60 and remained within 0.01 of the best comparator at budgets 75-120.

title: Melting noncoplanar order on the square-kagome lattice: Chiral, flat-band, and staggered spin liquids from projective symmetry
abstract: Noncoplanar magnetic orders carry a scalar spin chirality, and their melting by quantum fluctuations has been proposed as a route to chiral spin liquids. We ask what this route can produce on the square-kagome lattice, where couplings across the octagons stabilize noncoplanar cuboc and conical orders. We classify the fermionic spin liquids of this lattice by their projective symmetry groups, identify the symmetry class into which each noncoplanar order would melt, and compare candidate states with Gutzwiller-projected wave functions. A magnetic selection rule constrains the route: the chirality of every cuboc and conical order alternates in space, so a liquid that keeps the symmetry of its parent order has zero Chern number and no spontaneous thermal Hall response. A Chern state can descend only from uniformly chiral orders, and the regular ones we find need ferromagnetic bow-tie couplings. The energetics do not favor a chiral liquid either: among the projected wave functions we compare, a cuboc1-ordered state is lowest for strong cross-octagon couplings, and nonchiral states, a valence-bond crystal or a time-reversal-symmetric liquid, for weaker ones. The two inequivalent site orbits shape the spinons: a relative time-reversal sign between them pins flat bands to the Fermi level, and because the translations of $p4mm$ are not commutators, staggered chiral liquids exist, which are absent on sixfold-symmetric lattices.

title: Pulse: Long-Horizon Tasks Need Streaming Personalization
abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake complex, long-horizon tasks that benefit from sustained personalized support through long-term memory. Existing memory-augmented methods retrieve and use memory primarily from the initial request, with limited awareness of ongoing execution and emerging personalization needs. Agents may therefore overlook user preferences and project constraints during multistep tasks. We propose Pulse, a streaming personalization method for long-horizon tasks. An independent, lightweight memory agent continuously monitors execution, identifies emerging personalization needs and potential preference conflicts, and uses user and project memories to provide targeted interventions at appropriate stages. Reinforcement learning optimizes when and how the memory agent intervenes, improving the timeliness and accuracy of personalized support. Pulse scores 71.9% on $π$-Bench and 46.4% on MCP-Persona, achieving the highest overall scores among the compared methods on both datasets while improving task execution efficiency.

title: Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent for Radiation Therapy Treatment Planning
abstract: Direct incorporation of dose-volume constraints into inverse radiotherapy planning leads to large mixed-integer optimization problems that accurately represent clinical requirements but are computationally challenging. We develop and evaluate a quantum-inspired approach for automated dose-volume-constrained intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) planning. Clinical requirements are formulated as mixed-integer optimization problems, with binary variables representing dose-volume constraint violations. Patient-specific dose-influence matrices are generated at the photon control-point and proton spot levels, and intensities are optimized using Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent (QIHD). We evaluate QIHD on eight clinical cases: four IMRT (two prostate, one head-and-neck, and one liver) and four IMPT (two lung, one prostate, and one liver). The IMRT formulations contain 27,621 to 112,565 variables and are solved in 5 to 32 minutes, while the IMPT formulations contain 69,861 to 221,342 variables and are solved in 11 to 35 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU. QIHD produces dose distributions satisfying clinical protocols without manual intervention. In comparison, a CPU implementation of Gurobi fails to solve most tested mixed-integer formulations within several hours. These results demonstrate the computational feasibility of GPU-accelerated QIHD for automated photon and proton treatment planning. Prospective clinical validation and implementation of decomposed subproblems on quantum hardware remain future directions.

title: Galois Actions on Energy-Harmonic Functions
abstract: We study the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on the solutions to the discrete Dirichlet problem for a graph with fixed edge energies. We establish transitivity of the Galois action outside a thin set in the parameter space and demonstrate that the exceptional thin set may be Zariski dense, so the conclusion cannot in general be replaced by one that holds on a Zariski-open set. Identifying the parameter locus where the Galois action is transitive constrains the possibilities for linking combinatorial and arithmetic properties of the discrete energy-harmonic Laplace equations and other systems of the same form.

title: Quantum Generalized Cluster Algebras from Scattering Diagrams: Positivity and Mutation
abstract: We construct generalized quantum cluster scattering diagrams over a ring of formal reciprocal exchange coefficients, for compatible seeds satisfying \(\widetilde B^TΛ=[I_n\mid0].\) A central lattice extension records the roots of the exchange polynomials as independent degrees. Applying Davison--Mandel positivity in this extension and proving a positive cylinder projection theorem yields positive wall factorizations and theta coefficients in the root variables. Their regular classical limits recover generalized cluster scattering diagrams. Nonvanishing under classical specialization, together with control of the mutated positive monoids, gives quantum mutation compatibility. The resulting scattering atlas has the generalized cluster fan, and every reachable cluster monomial is a theta function. Classical detection of theta coefficients gives a geometric proof of the Laurent phenomenon, with positivity after adjoining the polynomial roots. Evaluation of the exchange coefficients recovers the generalized quantum cluster algebras with this normalization. The Fock--Goncharov mutation product becomes a wall-crossing action, identifying extended \(g\)-vectors with leading theta exponents and \(F\)-polynomials with the coefficient factors on their right. Constructing these polynomials before evaluation gives the separation formula for arbitrary prescribed reciprocal Laurent polynomial coefficients, without requiring positivity at \(t=1.\) Positivity in the roots is distinguished throughout from positivity in the exchange coefficients.

title: Equivalence of superintegrable Poisson projection chains: magnetic cotangent bundles and spin Calogero-Moser models
abstract: We study superintegrable Hamiltonian systems in terms of Poisson projection chains and their (spectral) equivalence. We compare two reduction constructions: (i) the cotangent bundle $T^*(G/A)$, $A=Z_G(γ)$, with the magnetic symplectic form defined by the orbit $G\cdot γ\cong G/A$, and (ii) the left-right Hamiltonian reduction of $T^*G$ that gives spin Calogero-Moser type systems. We prove that the two resulting chains are equivalent on an open set of regular points of principal orbit type: the phase spaces, the intermediate Poisson manifolds and the base spaces are identified compatibly with the projections. In particular, both constructions give the same commuting Hamiltonians.

title: A note on the product of holomorphic correspondences
abstract: In this article we study the concept of product of two holomorphic correspondences which was introduced in our previous work. Beginning with some basic results regarding the orbit space associated with the product correspondence, we then move on to a detailed analysis on the thermodynamic formalism of the same. Some of the results look at the behaviour of the product correspondence with respect to the individual correspondences. Finally, we explore different families of correspondences with expanding nature.

title: Subexponential-Time Exact-One Hitting Set
abstract: Exact-One Hitting Set is one of Karp's original 21 NP-complete problems: given an explicitly listed family of subsets of an $r$-element ground set, decide whether a subset meets every input set in exactly one element. Combining our reduction with the fixed-width exact-counting theorem of OpenAI (2026), we obtain a deterministic polynomial-space algorithm that computes the exact number of feasible selections in time $2^{O(r\log\log(r+16)/\sqrt{\log(r+16)})}\operatorname{poly}(L+1)=2^{o(r)}\operatorname{poly}(L+1)$, where $L$ is the input length. The number and widths of the input sets are unrestricted. Known row selection retains at most $r+1$ input constraints, but their total width may remain quadratic. Our path representation of two-query counting cancellation constructs two ordinary 3-CNF formulas with at most $2r$ variables and $O(r^2)$ clauses each, whose model counts differ by the desired answer. The auxiliary-variable budget depends on the number of simultaneous conditions, not on their widths or on the numbers of witnesses. We extend this construction to signed equations with fixed bounded demands and positive integer coefficients. We also represent every explicitly listed Boolean relation of VC dimension at most one by binary clauses and signed exact-one equations on its original variables, obtaining the same two-query variable bound for unrestricted overlaps among such local constraints. A bounded-term version further handles fixed finite/cofinite local degree rules on arbitrary graphs. The path representation is related by variable elimination to existing marker--parity cancellation.

title: Equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for amenable actions
abstract: We prove that every amenable action of a countable discrete group on a separable, simple, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra absorbs the trivial action on $\mathcal{Z}$ up to cocycle conjugacy. The group may be nonamenable, as in Suzuki's recent examples, and no assumptions on outerness or on the tracial state space are needed. This extends OpenAI's result for amenable groups to amenable actions. Amenability of the action cannot be omitted in general, as examples of the author and Lupini show. More generally, we show that every tracially amenable action on a separable, unital, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra with traces admits invariant central copies of all matrix algebras, without simplicity or nuclearity. For amenable actions on simple nuclear algebras, equivariant property (SI) allows one to deduce $\mathcal{Z}$-stability from this. As applications, we obtain absorption of $\mathcal{Z}$ for intermediate subalgebras in the crossed product, and also pure infiniteness for outer amenable actions of nonamenable groups. The basic techniques involving Gaussian variables originate in OpenAI's preprint, and are also the main new tool in its proposed solution to the Toms--Winter conjecture. We extend these techniques in order to deal with the weight functions coming from amenability, and one of the main new ingredients is the fact that one can replace an amenable action by an auxiliary one for which the amenability weights are central. In order to make the probabilistic tools accessible to the community beyond what is used here, we include an appendix where the theory is developed assuming only an elementary background, and where the relevant estimates are proved in detail.

title: Source shapes in coordinate and momentum space in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}$ = 200 GeV Au+Au collisions
abstract: In high-energy heavy-ion physics, femtoscopy aims to explore and understand the space-time characteristics of the collisions through investigating the correlation function of particle pairs. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown that the shape of the particle source function can be well described by the Lévy distribution, motivating further phenomenological studies. In this work, we perform a three-dimensional analysis of the source shapes for different particle-pair types in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}=200$ GeV Au+Au collisions generated with the EPOS event generator. In contrast to our previous analyses, where we fitted the one-dimensional projections of the pair distribution function, $D(ρ_j)$ ($j \in \{\text{out}, \text{side}, \text{long}\}$), now we reconstruct the three-dimensional $C(\boldsymbol{q})$ correlation function and fit it directly, as in experimental analyses. Furthermore, we now apply full three-dimensional fits instead of fitting the one-dimensional projections. We find that this approach results in smaller Lévy index values, while the direction averaged Lévy scale and the correlation strength remain largely unchanged, except for kaons. In the case of pions, the $α$ values are closer to the PHENIX data, showing a good agreement above 20\% centrality.

title: Canonical quantum curve I
abstract: We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat HΨ_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $Ψ_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients. These corrections depend only on closed moduli and $\hbar$ and vanish classically. Whenever a geometric definition is available, we conjecture that the corrected coefficients are suitably normalized Wilson-loop expectation values. When a corresponding refined theory exists, we conjecture a relation between the canonical vanishing point and the closed Nekrasov--Shatashvili free energy. We prove the quantum curve conjecture for Weierstrass curves and the mirror curves of canonical bundles of smooth projective toric weak del Pezzo surfaces, including local $\mathbb P^2$. For the local surfaces considered here, we relate the canonical vanishing point to a derivative of the closed NS free energy. For local $\mathbb P^2$, we also identify the corrected coefficient with a suitably normalized, geometrically defined NS Wilson-loop expectation value.

title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and localized boundary data $ψ(x')ϕ(t)\mathbf e_j$, $1\le j\le n$, where $ψ$ is supported in the closed unit ball. A separation point is a boundary point outside $\operatorname{supp}ψ$ where a component takes both signs on positive-measure sets in every sufficiently small adjoining space-time neighborhood. By evaluating the spatial convolutions appearing in the solution formula of the Stokes system via confluent hypergeometric functions, we obtain explicit formulas for the first normal derivatives of tangential components, the second normal derivative of the normal component, and tangential pressure derivatives at the boundary. For normal data, suitable Hölder regularity and strict log-concavity of $ϕ$ yield a unique separation point for each tangential component at every point of its coordinate axis outside the ball, and exactly two for the normal component at each sufficiently distant boundary point. We prove monotonicity and large-distance asymptotics of their temporal coordinates and quantitative temporal vanishing estimates for the normal derivatives. For tangential data in $n\ge3$, we prove the existence and uniqueness of separation points of tangential and normal components, including at fixed spatial points while $ϕ$ is positive. We derive spatial asymptotics at large distance and time from data moments and, under a geometric condition, supporting faces of $\operatorname{supp}ψ$. We characterize tangential pressure-gradient signs for both tangential and normal data, locating favorable and adverse regions near the boundary. For radial $ψ$, additional assumptions yield existence, uniqueness, and asymptotics of pressure-gradient zeros and zero curves, including those governed by the zero of the Caputo half-derivative of $ϕ$.

title: ISBC: Interpretable Sparse Binary Coding of Pretrained Text Embeddings
abstract: Pretrained text embeddings encode semantic structure in high-dimensional continuous spaces whose coordinates are difficult to interpret. We introduce Interpretable Sparse Binary Coding (ISBC), which learns a small set of binary dimensions from frozen embeddings without taxonomy labels or downstream outcomes. A trainable encoder and affine decoder combine reconstruction with controls on activity, factor utilization, dependence, and activation uncertainty. Individual bits and their conjunctions select overlapping document groups; complete activation profiles provide finer contexts for conditional comparisons. We evaluate these representations across corpora, backbones, and code configurations through reconstruction, geometry, predictive probes, and document inspection. Empirical cases identify both distinctions within existing categories and shared content across their boundaries. In a mixed-domain corpus, the most frequent profiles predominantly identify source collections, while selected within-source comparisons reveal sentiment and migration contrasts. Selected associations persist in additional documents encoded without refitting. In an engagement application, bits alone improve prediction of log-transformed outcomes over a constant reference, while their combinations identify within-event content contrasts associated with engagement. The results support using binary coordinates and their combinations for empirical interpretation, with complete profiles providing a fine, partly initialization-dependent description rather than a unique discrete taxonomy.

title: Probing the nature of Galactic microquasars with diffuse gamma rays and neutrinos: low-mass versus high-mass X-ray binaries
abstract: The observations of sub-PeV gamma-ray emission have provided strong evidence for a Galactic origin of the cosmic-ray "knee" region. Meanwhile, mounting observations have ruled out most supernova remnants as sources of PeV cosmic rays, i.e., the so-called PeVatrons. Recently, a new type of PeVatron candidate, microquasars, has received much attention. Studies indicate that microquasars could be the dominant contributor to PeV cosmic rays. However, the spatial distribution of microquasars is not known. They could belong to either LMXBs or HMXBs, depending on the mass of the optical companion star. In this work, we study which type could be the dominant by means of very high energy gamma rays and neutrinos. We find that the diffuse gamma-ray distributions along the Galactic longitude are quite different due to the spatial distributions of these two kinds of sources. If the very high energy gamma rays are dominated by the distribution of LMXBs, the gamma-ray distribution would be more concentrated toward the direction of the Galactic center. Furthermore, we also find that HMXB distribution cannot account for the latest observations of Galactic diffuse neutrinos. Higher-precision measurements of the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino fluxes with LHAASO, HAWC, IceCube, and KM3NeT will allow the spatial distribution of the microquasar population to be determined and the origin of the knee to be tested.

title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

title: Stratified Superintegrability of Spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland Systems
abstract: We study the Poisson chain of the compact spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland system obtained by conjugation reduction of $T^*\mathrm{SU}(n)$ at a fixed coadjoint orbit. We give a Horn-type condition ensuring that the spectral torus acts freely on the full fiber over a simple spectrum; for each orbit, the admissible spectra form a nonempty open dense set, and the restricted chain is strongly superintegrable of rank $n-1$ on every orbit-type stratum. We also construct, across certain affine spectral walls, a proper quotient map onto a Hausdorff stratified Poisson space with a finite Whitney stratification. For $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, we compute the free spectral domain and the quotient near two intersecting walls, and a zero-orbit example shows that the analogous quotient need not be Hausdorff on the unrestricted reduced phase space.

title: Robust distortion riskmetrics under symmetry, unimodality, and Wasserstein constraints
abstract: We study worst-case distortion riskmetrics over symmetric distributions with prescribed mean and variance in a Wasserstein ball around a reference distribution. Our key contribution is the construction of a reference-dependent auxiliary distortion that encodes the Wasserstein constraint while preserving symmetry under the concave-envelope operation. Under suitable regularity and nondegeneracy conditions, this construction yields sharp upper bounds for distortions of bounded variation, allowing nonmonotonicity and interior discontinuities, and identifies extremal distributions when the bounds are attained. An approximation preserving symmetry and the prescribed moments exactly shows that upper semicontinuous relaxation of the symmetrized distortion leaves the supremum unchanged for budgets strictly above the feasibility threshold. With additional unimodality, symmetry fixes the quantile's concavity-convexity transition at the midpoint, yielding a characterization via $L^2$-projection onto a fixed closed convex cone for absolutely continuous distortions with square-integrable derivatives. Numerical examples for ES, RVaR, and VaR illustrate how shape restrictions and the reference distribution affect feasibility and worst-case risk. Simulations with data-dependent Wasserstein radii examine worst-case ES and feasibility under correctly specified and misspecified shape restrictions.

title: Global classical solutions of the repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system
abstract: Global classical existence for general large data in the three-dimensional repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system has long been an open problem. We give an affirmative answer: every nonnegative $C^1$ initial datum satisfying \[ f_0(x,p)+|\nabla_{x,p}f_0(x,p)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-a}\langle p\rangle^{-b},\qquad a>1,\quad b>3, \] generates a unique global classical solution. No smallness or symmetry is assumed. The result covers finite and infinite mass and energy, including infinite kinetic energy density. The power thresholds are sharp for general pure-power bounds ensuring finite density and an absolutely convergent Coulomb field. The proof rests on two new mechanisms: local energy recovery for a population selected by energy growth, and a corrected moment--action closure based on nonnegative transverse interactions. The argument also yields global classical solutions of the nonrelativistic equation in the same initial class, allowing infinite mass with polynomial velocity tails of any order $b>3$.

title: Positive expansiveness of operator semigroups: orbit growth and spectral criteria
abstract: This paper studies positive expansiveness and positive kinematic expansiveness for strongly continuous semigroups of bounded linear operators on complex Banach spaces. We prove that positive kinematic expansiveness is equivalent to the unboundedness of every nonzero orbit, while positive expansiveness additionally requires the generator to be bounded from below. We also show that continuous changes of time can be replaced by increasing homeomorphisms without changing positive expansiveness. Uniform exponential expansion implies positive expansiveness without any surjectivity assumption; we characterize it through the minimum modulus, the lower growth bound, and the approximate point spectrum of a single semigroup operator. Under a uniform positive lower bound on the semigroup, positive expansiveness is equivalent to positive kinematic expansiveness together with boundedness below of the generator. Diagonal semigroups on $\ell_p$ then show that uniform exponential expansion, positive expansiveness and its kinematic version form a strictly decreasing hierarchy. Finally, we derive necessary spectral conditions for bounded generators and show that all three properties coincide in finite dimensions.

title: Excited-state-induced nonlinearity and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent through a quantum dot
abstract: Quantum dots are electrically tuneable thermal machines capable of both energy harvesting and cooling at the nanoscale in the cryogenic regime. At large thermal biases, their thermoelectric transport shows a complex behaviour, including additional extrema and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent. Though these asymmetries and nonlinearities directly affect rectification and power conversion, their origin has not been studied systematically. We address this through measurements and modelling of a single GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dot whose source is heated by white-noise excitation. Using Pauli master equation for sequential tunnelling through a two-level dot, retaining the full Fermi distributions of both leads, distinct tunnel rates for the two levels, and relaxation between them, we show that the excited state acts as a second transport channel which competes with the ground-state contribution. Strong excited-state coupling combined with slow relaxation produces polarity reversals in the thermocurrent; without both, the excited state yields only additional extrema and an amplitude asymmetry across the charge degeneracy point. Experimentally, as the source temperature increases, an additional extremum emerges in the thermocurrent which develops into a polarity reversal. Using the excited-state level spacing and ground-state tunnel rate obtained independently from pulsed-gate and bias spectroscopies, the model reproduces the positions of the observed extrema and their amplitudes to within a factor of about three, placing the device in the regime of slow relaxation and strong excited-state coupling. Our results establish thermocurrent line-shape as a probe of excited-state tunnelling and relaxation in quantum dots. Excited states, often treated as a minor correction, can dominate quantum-dot thermoelectric transport far from equilibrium.

title: A Computational Verification of the Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for $z\leq 10^{500000}$
abstract: We describe a finite computational verification of Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for normalized positive integer solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ with $z \leq 10^{500000}$. The archived run reports $239\,536\,376\,556$ triples with distinct maximal coordinates.The method combines a disjoint tree decomposition, certified fixed-point range bounds, a deterministic 48-bit candidate screen,and replay modulo $2^{128}$. We give the mathematical justification and a reproducibility procedure covering package checks,retained-data auditing, and a full rerun. The conclusion depends on correct execution of the exhaustive screen and replay; the retained audit does not regenerate the deleted screening buckets.

title: On motivic multiplicativity of cyclic covers
abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$ with trivial Chow groups, and let $f: X\rightarrow Y$ be a cyclic cover of degree $d$ branched over a smooth ample divisor $D\in |dL|$. We show that a naturally constructed Chow--Künneth decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for each integer $m\geq2$ and that its stable motivic multiplicativity defect satisfies $\mathfrak{sd}(X)\leq 2dn$. If, in addition, each positive-codimension cycle class on $Y$ is supported on $D$, then a double cover admits motivic $0$-multiplicativity. As a further application, we show that any smooth Gushel--Mukai sixfold admits motivic 0-multiplicativity. Moreover, we establish the sharp modified-diagonal property for all smooth double EPW sextics, confirming a conjecture of O'Grady for these varieties.

title: Active Jarzynski and Crooks Relations for Driven Jump-Diffusions
abstract: Non-conservative active driving breaks detailed balance in non-Gaussian jump-diffusions, obscuring the connection between external protocol work, housekeeping dissipation, and free-energy differences. Here, we establish exact finite-time fluctuation relations for driven Markov jump-diffusions---encompassing infinite-activity Lévy processes---by comparing path probabilities under the forward and current-reversed dual dynamics relative to the instantaneous steady state (ISS). We derive a trajectory-level decomposition of total entropy production that cleanly separates transient state relaxation, housekeeping heat, and external protocol driving. When the ISS takes a Gibbsian form, gauge-tilting the dual path measure yields an Active Jarzynski equality, $\langle\exp[-(W+Δs_{\mathrm{act}})]\rangle_{π_0}=e^{-ΔF}$, which incorporates active housekeeping entropy $Δs_{\mathrm{act}}$ alongside mechanical work $W$ and coexists with the conventional Jarzynski equality. Under protocol reversal, this dual framework further reveals an Active Crooks relation, where the asymmetry between forward and reverse work distributions is governed by the conditional exponential average of active dissipation. Our results provide a framework for recovering free-energy differences in driven jump-diffusions with Gibbsian instantaneous steady states and for characterizing active irreversibility through trajectory statistics.

title: Burning limits and the role of small scale turbulence in high Karlovitz number premixed flames
abstract: Premixed flames exhibit a progressive enhancement in burning rates with turbulence, with the ultimate limits governed by the onset of local extinctions. Piloted premixed burners have enabled access to turbulence far exceeding the theoretically predicted extinction limits, with the measured flame speeds still improving. This study explores the role of small scale turbulence on the burning rates of premixed flames using a piloted high Karlovitz number burner. Premixed CH$_4$-air mixtures with equivalence ratios ($ϕ$) from 0.7--1.0, stabilized using a $ϕ$-matched pilot flame, were subjected to increasing rms fluctuating velocities, $u'$, up to 36.0 m/s. The experimental setup enables a progressive increase in turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) at smaller scales, with the Kolmogorov scales reaching approximately 4 $μ$m under the highest turbulence condition. Global consumption flame speeds, $S_\mathrm{T,GC}$, derived from the binarized Planar Laser-Induced Fluorescence (PLIF) imaging of OH radicals, scale with turbulent diffusivity, $\mathcal{D}_\mathrm{T}$. Further increases in $u'$, however, lead to a maximum and an eventual decline in flame speeds. The measured flame speeds exhibit a common scaling with the measured upstream $u'$. Assessments of the flame structure using CH-PLIF images further reveal progressive straining and extinction events with increasing $u'$ despite flames maintaining their flamelet-like appearance, suggesting that the observed limits derive from the increasing extinction propensity across the flame front. Finally, these findings are incorporated into a scaling relation accounting for the role of straining and extinctions in the observed flame-speed trends.

title: Leap-VLA: High-Rate Robot Control from a Low-Rate VLM Backbone
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models re-encode the full observation through a multi-billion-parameter vision-language model (VLM) at every control step, even though scene semantics evolve at roughly 1 Hz while reactive control requires 20-50 Hz. We present a VLA that decouples the two: a VLM runs as a low-frequency semantic anchor whose cached context is reused across control steps, while a flow-matching action expert operates at high frequency, consuming the cached semantics with a fresh, low-latency visual stream from a compact encoder pretrained on robot video with masked reconstruction, optical flow, and depth. The measured age $τ$ of the cache conditions the expert through adaptive layer normalization. Reusing the cache makes the policy a function of its age, and training covers that function explicitly: cache ages sampled from real episode history, plus an age-ramped pixel corruption that erases the stale snapshot the way deployed staleness corrupts content. On the asynchronous deployment stack, the recipe closes most of the staleness gap: on LIBERO-Spatial, 61.4% to 95.5% at a 2 s semantic refresh (95.9% at 1 s, within 1.6 points of the frequency-matched anchor); averaged over the four LIBERO suites, the deployed policy holds 95.2% at a 1 s refresh and 94.5% at 2 s against a 96.3% matched anchor. A forward-only chunk-boundary correction (soft-nudge), an autograd-free reformulation of real-time-chunking guidance, carries per-control-step re-planning without loss (97.1%) at zero added latency. The same lens exposes a second defect: under an instruction-scene mismatch the policy keeps manipulating the scene, and a chain-of-thought verdict gate trained on zero-cost negative episodes freezes execution exactly on mismatched instructions without hurting feasible success.

title: Mutual-visibility colouring with two colours is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that any two vertices of $S$ are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $χ_μ(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition $V(G)$. Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter $d$, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. The proof rests on a reformulation of $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the $2$-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from $2$-colourability of $3$-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.

title: Ground state uniqueness and quantitative stability for the mass-critical Hartree equation
abstract: We prove that the ground state of the mass-critical Hartree equation is unique up to phase rotations and translations and nondegenerate in every dimension $d\ge3$. This makes the recent conditional $L^2$ classification of minimal-mass blow-up and non-scattering solutions unconditional; we also give a direct $H^1$ proof of the finite-time blow-up classification. We further establish a global quadratic stability estimate for the sharp Hartree interpolation inequality. For the optimal stability constant, we rule out vanishing of minimizing sequences and describe their possible loss of compactness.

title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

title: IJev: Order-Invariant Decisions via Iterated Cyclic Reordering
abstract: System One decision models answer a choice question in one forward pass, but their answer depends on the order in which options are listed, and their probabilities carry a prior over answer labels. An invariant ordering operator is any fixed function that returns the same ordered option list for every input order of a fixed option set. Starting from any such order and averaging a listwise readout over its K cyclic shifts removes the input order, but the decision still depends on the chosen cyclic class: those $K$ shifts are only one of the (K-1)! classes, and different invariant operators can select different classes. We propose IJev, which repeatedly reorders the options by the cyclic-averaged, label-prior-corrected distribution and runs another cyclic average. Every iterate is exactly input-order-invariant. When the iteration does not converge, we average the round distributions rather than return the last round. On five benchmarks and five models, IJev has flip rate zero in every cell. The default uniform average over T=20 rounds substantially improves calibration over a single cyclic average, and its accuracy is comparable. A descriptive choice of horizon and averaging rule is best or tied-best for accuracy in all 25 settings.

title: Ground state and excitations of the \(C_2^{(1)}\) spin chain with non-diagonal boundaries
abstract: Understanding boundary effects in higher-rank integrable quantum spin chains requires connecting exact spectral relations with the root configurations underlying their energies and excitations. With non-diagonal boundaries, determining these configurations remains challenging even when an exact spectral solution is available, hindering the direct extraction of thermodynamic properties. We address this problem for the rational $C_2^{(1)}$ chain by combining DMRG in the tensor-network framework with the quantum inverse scattering method. The numerically determined zeros of the fundamental and fused transfer-matrix eigenvalues reveal three bulk-string distributions, labeled by $x$, $y$, and $w$, together with boundary strings and additional roots. Substituting these configurations into the operator identities relating the two transfer matrices yields the ground-state energy and the surface energy in the thermodynamic limit under non-diagonal boundary conditions. The analytical surface energy agrees with the numerical results up to $O(\tfrac1N)$ corrections. From the regularity conditions of the operator identities, we derive a boundary-string selection rule and numerically identify allowed configurations beyond the ground state. For excitations preserving the boundary-string configuration, we identify three elementary hole excitations, $X$, $Y$, and $W$, in the $x$-, $y$-, and $w$-string distributions, respectively, and derive their energies. Based on the symmetry of the zero roots, we also present a bulk-excitation selection rule governing the allowed combinations of these elementary excitations in physical eigenstates. The framework developed here can therefore be used to systematically analyze boundary effects, bulk excitations, and related physical properties in other high-rank integrable quantum models with non-diagonal boundary conditions.

title: Second-Order Least Squares Method for Statistical Inference in Linear Models with Asymmetric Errors
abstract: In a linear regression model with normal random errors, the ordinary least squares estimator is the most efficient estimator. However, when the random errors have an asymmetric distribution, a more efficient estimator can be constructed using the higher moments of the data. In this paper, we use the second-order least squares method to obtain more accurate asymptotic confidence intervals and more powerful hypothesis tests in linear models. We also develop an efficient and stable numerical algorithm to calculate the proposed estimator. Our extensive simulation studies demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method. Two real data examples are presented.

title: Robust Pixel-wise Digital Image Correlation under Large Motions and Illumination Variations via a Global-to-Local Hybrid Neural Field
abstract: Digital image correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact technique for full-field displacement measurement. Data-driven deep-learning DIC offers rapid inference but may generalize poorly to unseen speckle patterns, deformation modes, noise levels, and illumination conditions. Classical optimization-based DIC and recent image-constrained neural formulations avoid labeled displacement data, yet their convergence and accuracy remain vulnerable to initialization, large rigid-body motion, fine non-uniform deformation, and gray-value disturbances. This paper presents a global-to-local hybrid neural DIC framework for robust pixelwise measurement. Stage 1 estimates a dominant in-plane rigid transformation through coarse rotation search, phase correlation, and masked refinement, providing a reliable initialization under large translation and rotation. Stage 2 represents the residual displacement with a hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), and optimizes it using a valid-overlap, illumination-robust structural loss. The local gray-value model explicitly accommodates multiplicative and additive intensity changes. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate accurate and stable displacement recovery under noise, non-uniform deformation, large rotation, illumination variation, and degraded imaging conditions.

title: Inverse source problem of variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equations
abstract: This paper investigates an inverse temporal source problem for a variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equation with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. By the perturbation method, the model is equivalently transformed into a constant-order fractional diffusion equation with a convolution perturbation term. Existence, uniqueness, and energy estimates of strong and weak solutions to the forward problem are established, and for a separable source term the uniqueness and Lipschitz stability of the temporal source function are proved using local integral observations. A numerical reconstruction algorithm combining Tikhonov regularization with the conjugate gradient method is developed with a convergence error estimate, and numerical experiments verify its effectiveness and stability for different variable-exponent functions, noise levels and source functions. Since fractional advection--diffusion models describe the turbulent transport of airborne pollutants, the method is also applicable in atmospheric science for recovering the emission history of a pollution source from sparse measurements.

title: Spanning tree with bounded degree sum of two adjacent vertices
abstract: In this paper, we first give a sharp sufficient condition on degree sum for a connected graph to have a spanning tree whose maximum of degree sum of two adjacent vertices are bounded. These improve some previous results on the spanning tree with bounded maximum degree. Next, we also use our main result to study the generalized rainbow connection of graphs. In particular, we give some degree sum conditions for a connected graphs to have a bounded (1,2)- rainbow connection number.

title: Stability of least-energy solutions of the harmonic map flow from the plane into the 2-sphere
abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of the least-energy harmonic map $W:\mathbb R^2\to S^2$ for the harmonic map flow under small, sufficiently decaying, non-symmetric perturbations. Solutions exist globally and are asymptotically described by a modulation of $W$ plus a remainder that converges to zero as $t\to\infty$. The modulation parameters associated with scaling, rotation, and translation remain close to their initial values and converge to finite limits. The proof relies on an inner-outer gluing decomposition and the analysis of a non-local equation governing the modulation parameters.

title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
abstract: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations.
