Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed in exactly this way; a tempered statistic, selected on synthetic data and registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field ($E\approx 1.1\times10^{10}$). Every analysis is preregistered, fixed in a dated protocol before it was run, or labelled exploratory, and every reported result is generated from hashed result files.

title: Generalized Principal Eigenvalues of Spatially Periodic Nonlocal Operators with Applications to Noncooperative KPP Systems
abstract: In this paper, we study generalized principal eigenvalues of the spatially periodic cooperative nonlocal operator $\mathcal{L}\boldsymbolφ=\mathcal{J}*\boldsymbolφ -\boldsymbolφ+A(x)\boldsymbolφ$ and their applications to noncooperative KPP systems. In the periodic setting, we characterize the existence of a classical principal eigenvalue and explicitly construct and classify Radon measure solutions to the associated eigenproblem when a positive continuous principal eigenfunction does not exist. On the whole space, we consider two notions of generalized principal eigenvalues defined through positive test functions and characterize them through a family of weighted periodic spectral values and Dirichlet approximations. For large spatial periods, we identify the spectral limits through a scalar Hamilton--Jacobi cell problem and, under additional assumptions, derive leading-order corrections and eigenfunction concentration results. For small spatial periods, we characterize the limits by an averaged operator and obtain refined expansions for specific classes of kernels, including formulas for the difference between the two whole-space generalized principal eigenvalues. Finally, we apply the spectral theory to establish extinction and persistence criteria for the associated noncooperative KPP systems, characterize spreading speeds along rays by a Freidlin--Gärtner-type formula, and study their asymptotic behavior as the spatial period tends to infinity or zero.

title: Muography Simulations for Carbon Capture and Storage Monitoring
abstract: Muography can monitor CO2 storage through reservoir density changes, but site-scale simulations are costly: reservoirs can be deep and borehole detectors are small. We address both with two approaches. First, a two-stage workflow splits the kilometer-scale simulation: a fast code transports muons through the overburden, and a general-purpose Monte Carlo code through the reservoir and detectors. Second, a geometric filter at the source keeps only muons whose direction and position let them reach the detectors, within a margin for multiple scattering, and a range cut removes those with too little energy. Both are available in the UCMuon simulation suite for muon generation, filtering and transport. At a deep (800-1000 m) and a shallow (65 m) CO2 storage site, each approach reduces the computing time about 700-fold, and the filtered simulation gives the same hit rate as a full one, as long as the margin exceeds the muons' sideways scattering drift.

title: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
abstract: GPTQ is Babai's nearest-plane algorithm on the lattice of the Cholesky factor of the layer's input second moment $Σ$. In the high-rate, entropy-coded regime it needs $\tfrac12\log_2(\AM/\GM)$ of its Cholesky pivots more bits than WaterSIC, which is within $0.255$ bit of the rate-distortion limit for every $Σ$; random rotations close most of this gap in practice, and Ordentlich and Polyanskiy asked for the worst-case gap between rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC. We show that after a Haar rotation the $k$-th pivot converges almost surely, uniformly in $k\geδn$ and over spectra $ν$ of bounded condition number, to $1/S_ν(-k/n)$, a classical formula from the theory of Lyapunov exponents, and use it to answer the question. Over spectra with condition number $κ$ the worst rotated gap is $\tfrac12\log_2κ-\log_2\lnκ+\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\ln2}+o(1)$ bits, attained only by two-point spectra, just $\tfrac12\log_2\lnκ+O(1)$ bits below the worst case without rotation, so rotation cannot replace waterfilling in general. It nearly can on real layers: rotation cuts the cost of an $η$-fraction of outlier eigenvalues of size $μ$ from about $ημ$ to $η^2μ/2$ to leading order, but cannot remove spectral spread on a logarithmic scale; for non-Gaussian weights it also adds a weight-side rate cost, which we characterize exactly under a standard high-rate assumption. On $96$ Hessians of Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 the rotated gap has median $0.04$ bit and maximum $0.36$ bit, against $2$--$5$ bits in the worst case for the same condition numbers, and the limit matches it to within $0.009$ bit.

title: Aperture Photometric Accuracy of Point-spread-function-deconvolved Astronomical Images
abstract: This paper introduces an improved Richardson--Lucy (RL) framework utilizing negative backfilling (NB) and the novel filtered image deconvolution and noise backfilling (FiDNoBa) algorithm. By integrating a low-pass prefiltering stage---specifically employing a Kalman filter---with the reintegration of filtered-out noise components after RL iterations, we effectively suppress noise artifacts while maintaining rigorous flux integrity. We extensively evaluate our Kalman + RL + NB approach using both numerical simulations and real observational data. Simulations across three regimes demonstrate superior photometric accuracy, reducing the relative mean deviation (RMD) to below 1\% for isolated sources, maintaining high fidelity (RMD $\sim$0.37\%) for blended Sérsic galaxies, and achieving $\sim$5\% RMD in crowded stellar fields while significantly increasing source recovery rates compared to traditional point-spread function photometry. Crucially, we validate the practical efficacy of FiDNoBa on real space-based (JWST/NIRCam) and ground-based (Very Large Telescope Survey Telescope OmegaCAM) images. The results confirm that our method reliably handles complex instrumental signatures, such as the extended wings of the STPSF, mitigating the severe ringing artifacts typical of traditional RL deconvolution while ensuring highly stable aperture photometry in practical survey processing.

title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
abstract: We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.

title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

title: From Rock Tumbling to Telescope Mirror Grinding: How Optical Perfection Emerges from Random Motion
abstract: When two glass disks are rubbed together by hand with an abrasive between them, their surfaces spontaneously converge to perfectly matching spherical curves, accurate to tens of nanometers. How does such optical precision emerge from an essentially random manual process? Starting from Preston's law of material removal, we derive a first-principles explanation. Symmetries of the grinding stroke imply that planes and spheres are the generic equilibria of the process. Their stability is governed by a hierarchy of timescales: small-scale irregularities decay exponentially on the grinding timescale $T_\text{grind}$, while large-scale deviations from a sphere diffuse away on the longer spherizing timescale $T_\text{sphere} \propto (R_\text{mirror}/R_\text{stroke})^2\, T_\text{grind}$. Gravity and finite disk size destabilize planar surfaces, but for sufficiently short strokes spheres remain stable ($T_\text{deform} \gg T_\text{sphere}$), with only their radius of curvature varying adiabatically. The same framework unifies telescope mirror grinding with everyday phenomena: rock tumbling (explaining why rotary tumbling rounds edges more than vibratory, and why neither produce spheres) and sanding (explaining why small flat surfaces inevitably round). These examples offer an accessible classroom context for stable and unstable equilibria, exponential relaxation, diffusion, multi-timescale analysis, and the emergence of the Laplacian operator from averaging over a local area.

title: Boolean Rank Nine for Polygons with 35 to 40 Vertices
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the rectangle covering number, or Boolean rank, of every polygon slack matrix of order 35 through 40 is nine. The upper bound is due to Goucha, Gouveia, and Silva; the new contribution is the matching lower bound. A hypothetical covering by eight rectangles yields a saturated inclusion cycle between two antichains on eight coordinates. An exact maximal-chain identity bounds its length and assigns a nonnegative penalty to each inclusion edge. The equality case is excluded combinatorially, leaving at most 39 lower vertices. For orders 35 through 39, symmetry reductions and a shadow bound leave fifteen finite exclusions, each supported by a checked reverse-unit-propagation refutation. The main text presents the mathematical reductions and their dependencies; the accompanying supplement gives the complete cycle parameters, encodings, and certificate record. The previously known equality for orders 41 through 55 is cited directly.

title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. Benchmarking under the same measurement budget demonstrates substantially higher reconstruction fidelity than other encoding strategies, highlighting the advantages of learned optical compression. With the optical encoder fixed, decoder-only neural adaptation enables experimental transfer to previously unseen data distributions, extending the utility of the learned measurement representation. These results establish learned optical compression as a measurement-efficient and reusable framework for QPI, integrating phase-information compression into single-pixel intensity measurements while retaining adaptability to new data. This approach paves the way for low-data-rate phase imaging and sensing, with the potential to extend QPI to spectral regions where high-quality detector arrays are costly or unavailable.

title: MMCoT$^3$: Empowering 3D Scene Understanding with 3D-Text Interleaved Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
abstract: Understanding and reasoning over 3D scenes from point clouds is essential for a broad range of AI applications. Recent 3D large language models have shown promising results, yet they still face two fundamental limitations: (i) insufficient capability for grounded multi-step reasoning in complex 3D scenes, and (ii) a text-centric inference paradigm that lacks effective interaction between textual reasoning and visual evidence. As a result, these models often fail to verify intermediate inferences, disambiguate similar object instances, and avoid hallucinations. To address these limitations, we propose MMCoT$^3$, the first 3D-Text Interleaved Chain-of-Thought (CoT) framework for 3D scene understanding. The core idea is to explicitly interleave textual reasoning with task-relevant 3D evidence, enabling the model to consult scene observations throughout the reasoning process. In addition, since a textual mention in 3D scenes may correspond to multiple candidate objects, naive object-mention alignment can inject incorrect evidence and mislead subsequent reasoning. To mitigate this multi-instance ambiguity, we design an ambiguity-aware evidence aggregation mechanism that uses query-guided cross-attention to fuse candidate object tokens and inject both evidence and ambiguity cues into the reasoning process. To better equip the model with multi-step reasoning capability, we further develop PointCoT, a large-scale 3D-specific CoT instruction tuning dataset with approximately 176.2K instances spanning captioning, question answering, dialogue, and planning tasks. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks show that our method consistently improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art results, validating the effectiveness of our proposed ambiguity-aware 3D-text interleaved reasoning for 3D scene understanding.

title: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0: Causal World Models for Real-World Driving and Embodied Intelligence
abstract: We present Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0, a unified streaming causal world model for Physical AI. It models and generates causal physical evolution in the real world, and unifies heterogeneous conditioning inputs for view-consistent generation. The architecture integrates View-Temporal Attention (VTA) to capture cross-view spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics, together with Multi-view Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) to encode positional relationships across views and time. WorldRec 2.0 reconstructs static and dynamic 3D Gaussians from multi-view, multi-temporal observations in a single forward pass and uses their renderings as explicit scene context to preserve geometry and appearance during long-horizon generation. Conditioning inputs are fused through VAE latent concatenation in a shared representation space. We incorporate Gated Linear Attention (GLA) into the temporal layers of VTA for efficient streaming inference, reducing computation and KV-cache memory during multi-view rollouts. A physical-interaction data pipeline covers diverse interactions and long-tailed events. From Pre-train onward, these data are combined with large-scale videos and heterogeneous visual modalities to learn visual, geometric, and dynamic priors. During Mid-train, training across diverse view configurations further improves the model's ability to capture how actions and object states shape subsequent scene evolution. After distillation-based Post-train, we apply the model to closed-loop simulation, closed-loop training, and World Action Model (WAM) applications. These applications generate physically consistent future states and support world-state prediction, policy learning, and action generation for Physical AI.

title: Communication with Adversarial Users: Byzantine Models in Multi-User Information Theory
abstract: We consider communication systems operating in environments where some participating users cannot be trusted. This motivates the study of Byzantine communication models, in which users may behave adversarially. In this survey, we provide a unified information-theoretic perspective on communication with adversarial users in multi-user settings. We review recent advances in Byzantine multiple access channels, including reliable communication, adversary identification, and distributed function computation. Furthermore, we discuss extensions to classical-quantum channels and highlight fundamental differences between classical and quantum models. Finally, we outline key open problems and future research directions at the intersection of communication, computation, and security.

title: Bounds and sufficient conditions in quantum Zeno effect
abstract: When a quantum system undergoes a series of repeated measurements during its time evolution to check whether it remains in the initial state, the resulting state lifetime can decrease (the quantum Zeno effect) or increase (the quantum inverse Zeno effect) as the inter-measurement period increases. Several transitions between these two regimes may occur within the same system. A carefully chosen measurement period $τ_\ast$ (or rate $r_\ast$ in the case of a stochastic measurement protocol) brings the state lifetime to its global minimum. Here, we describe the upper and lower bounds on the optimized state lifetime, which are expressed in terms of characteristic time scales encoded in the state survival probability $P(T)$, which is assumed to decrease monotonically to zero at large $T$. In addition, we analyze the bounds on the optimal measurement periods/rates and formulate sufficient conditions for observing the inverse Zeno effect. The analysis is also extended to states with non-monotonic survival functions. The results are illustrated numerically with an example of a system of optically trapped ultra-cold atoms.

title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. Second, physics-informed methods impose a specified physical equation as a reconstruction constraint, but often require environment-dependent parameters that are difficult to acquire. As a result, practical 3D acoustic field reconstruction that is both physically grounded and robust to uncertain environmental information remains largely unexplored. This work takes an alternative route: instead of solving a fully specified wave equation, it extracts a structured representation from wave physics and learns its components from data. From the Helmholtz equation and normal mode propagation, we derive a structured spatial-angular tensor representation, termed the S/c representation. Under a low-rank specialization, it takes the form of a rank-(L,L,1) block-term tensor decomposition, which connects structured sampling patterns/routes used in ocean sensing to sufficient conditions for field recovery. Building on this tensor representation, we propose TIDAL, a neural reconstructor that uses the S/c representation as an inductive bias for structured decoding and aligns information aggregation with the sampling geometry. The neural learner removes the need for known model parameters required by conventional physics-based recovery methods. Experiments across three structured sampling geometries show that TIDAL achieves the best reconstruction performance and fastest inference among baselines, with benefits from the physics-derived representation under limited data and model capacity.

title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. Energetic electrons deposit energy in silicon, producing nonequilibrium carriers that perturb the semiconductor surface potential and electric displacement across the adjacent aqueous interface. The resulting redistribution of interfacial water polarization drives a transient compensation current, whereas carrier relaxation restores the initial polarization state and generates an opposite-polarity recovery signal. The complete irradiation-detector-electrometer system exhibits exponential rise and recovery time constants of approximately 1.0 and 3.6 ms, respectively. The response is strongly regulated by water-layer thickness and ionic composition, and the 17 beam pulses of a programmed 1 s sequence at 17 Hz are resolved individually. Integration with Ce:YAG further introduces a scintillation-mediated excitation pathway. These findings establish interfacial water polarization as a tunable, zero-bias electrical transduction mechanism for time-resolved beta-radiation monitoring and motivate future investigations of higher-energy charged particles and secondary particles relevant to neutrino detection.

title: Leveraging 2D Foundation Priors for Generalized Category Discovery under Test-Time Adaptation in 3D LiDAR Segmentation
abstract: In autonomous driving, 3D LiDAR semantic segmentation is expected to adapt to evolving environments and recognize previously unseen categories, making generalized category discovery under test-time adaptation (GCD-TTA) an important problem. However, existing works treat GCD and TTA separately, while the limited semantic information in 3D point clouds makes GCD-TTA under domain shift more prone to feature collapse when combining GCD with TTA. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage framework for GCD-TTA in 3D LiDAR semantic segmentation. Specifically, in the first stage, we adaptively aggregate local 3D features according to geometric density variations and obtain reliable pseudo labels under a global class-wise prototype consistency constraint. In the second stage, we cast category discovery as an optimal transport assignment process for globally consistent grouping of novel categories. Meanwhile, semantic features from 2D vision foundation models are fused with 3D point cloud features to enrich 3D semantic information and promote a more separable feature space. Extensive experiments on Synth4D to SemanticKITTI, SynLiDAR to SemanticKITTI, and Synth4D to nuScenes demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our method achieves the best overall mIoU on 9 out of 10 benchmark splits and improves the overall mIoU by up to 12.21 points over the strongest re-implemented baseline.

title: Accounting for correlations in the $ωπ$ spectral function and its implication on the leading model dependent contribution to the $τ^- \to π^-π^0 ν_τγ$ decay
abstract: The $ωπ$ spectral function, measured in the decay $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ by the CLEO Collaboration, is described in the vector meson dominance approach. We sample the parameter space using a Metropolis Monte-Carlo algorithm and generate a set of parameters of the corresponding form factor, explicitly accounting for the correlation among them. We show the improvement in the uncertainty region of the spectral function with respect to neglecting correlations. We test the conserved vector current hypothesis by showing the agreement of the spectral function with the expected from the measurement of the cross section of $e^+e^- \to ωπ$ by the SND experiment, and the consistency of the branching ratio of the $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ decay with the value reported by the Particle Data Group. As an application, we consider the $ω$-channel of the $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τγ$ process, the leading model dependent contribution in the vector meson dominance approach. We compute the contribution to the long distance electromagnetic correction function $G_\text{EM}(t)$, of the pure $ω$-channel and its interference with the structure independent part. We show that the uncertainties, using the set of correlated parameters, are largely reduced with respect to neglecting correlations. The implication on the isospin symmetry breaking correction to the muon magnetic dipole moment estimation from tau data is found to be consistent with previous results but with improved precision.

title: GaitFM: A Cross-Modal Foundation Model for Wearable Gait Assessment
abstract: Gait assessment supports the diagnosis, monitoring, and prognosis of diverse movement-related conditions, such as neurological and musculoskeletal disorders. Recent advances in deep learning using everyday wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) offer an accessible and low-cost approach to automated gait assessment. However, IMU measurements vary substantially across individuals, body locations, and device configurations, while existing deep learning models are typically developed using small, homogeneous datasets for specific clinical tasks, limiting their robustness and generalizability in diverse real-world contexts. Here we present GaitFM, a cross-modal foundation model for gait assessment using IMU sensors. GaitFM improves the generalizability of gait assessment by transferring knowledge from large vision models and pretraining on unlabeled IMU sensor data. We pretrain GaitFM on a large curated dataset comprising about 4,000 participants and 1.23 million gait windows across diverse clinical and daily conditions, sensor modalities, and body locations. GaitFM demonstrates strong performance across 18 gait-related tasks, including 3 gait parameter estimation tasks, 14 disease and gait abnormality detection tasks, and 1 clinical outcome prediction task. Furthermore, GaitFM generalizes across different sensor configurations and body locations, including those commonly used in clinical settings and everyday wearable devices. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of transferring visual knowledge in improving sensor-based gait assessment performance, offering a new promising pathway for addressing data scarcity in the sensor and medical domains.

title: Assessing Temporal Dispersion of Time-Varying Channel at 38 GHz for Different Reference Signals
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of reference waveform selection on temporal dispersion estimation in a time-varying radio channel at 38 GHz. Three reference waveforms-numerically generated in MATLAB, measured through a conducted connection, and recorded in an anechoic chamber -are compared using the same wideband channel measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Their effects on the estimated power delay profiles (PDPs), mean delay, and root mean square (RMS) delay spread are evaluated. Despite noticeable differences in the time-domain and spectral characteristics of the reference waveforms, the resulting PDPs exhibit similar multipath structures, while the estimated temporal dispersion parameters show relatively small differences. The results indicate limited sensitivity to reference waveform selection under the investigated measurement conditions.

title: An Electrolyte Equation of State Based on openCOSMO-RS: From Aqueous Solutions to Non-Aqueous Systems
abstract: Predictive COSMO-RS-based electrolyte models such as COSMO-RS-ES describe electrolyte solutions from quantum-chemical information, but treat the liquid as incompressible and give no access to densities or pressure effects. This work presents openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi, to our knowledge the first open-source implementation of a predictive electrolyte equation of state based on openCOSMO-RS. It combines the COSMO-RS-based equation of state openCOSMO-RS-Phi with the ion interaction energies and the long-range term of COSMO-RS-ES, which is first refitted on the same simplified short range. With this refit, a dielectric decrement improves the mean ionic activity coefficients (MIAC), whereas a Born term counts the solvation of the ions a second time and is therefore left out. The equation of state then adds only volume, dispersion and temperature parameters of the ions, fitted to aqueous MIAC and densities. openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi reproduces COSMO-RS-ES in dilute aqueous solutions, improves on it in concentrated ones and also yields solution densities. Extrapolating from aqueous systems, it predicts the MIAC in water + cosolvent mixtures as accurately as the fitted COSMO-RS-ES, as well as the MIAC and bubble points of a benchmark database of water-alcohol-salt systems. Salting-out of organic components is not described as accurately, and salts come out too soluble in organic solvents. Overall, the interaction model developed for COSMO-RS-ES carries over to a large extent to an equation of state, which makes openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi a sound base model for further development, with ion transfer between solvents as a clear target for fitting to non-aqueous data.

title: Percentile oscillations and the intrinsic square function
abstract: Wilson's intrinsic square function tests the input against all the cancellative functions of a given smoothness, at every location and scale. We show that it is dominated pointwise by a sparse square function, whose coefficients are the percentile oscillations of the input modulo polynomials, at every polynomial order below the smoothness plus one. These coefficients are local sizes, which nevertheless retain essentially all the cancellation: the weighted norms of the sparse square function are equivalent to smooth grand maximal norms, for all $0<p<\infty$ and $A_\infty$ weights, with explicit dependence on the weight. These are weighted Hardy norms in the range allowed by the smoothness. Consequences include potential bounds, and weighted Hardy space estimates with the sharp factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$. For the derivatives of Calderón--Zygmund operators, we characterize the corresponding square function estimates by testing conditions on the polynomial symbols of their wavelet resolution. In the quadratic setting, the factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$ detects a transition from $\mathrm{BMO}$ testing conditions to vanishing symbols.

title: SEALECT: Scene-Conditioned Pose Priors for Plausible Maritime Vessel Retrieval
abstract: We address scene-conditioned object retrieval for compositional augmentation in maritime imagery, where strong geometric constraints make appearance-only retrieval produce physically implausible vessel insertions. We propose SEALECT, a retrieval framework that jointly models visual compatibility, vessel pose, scale, and scene geometry through a unified score combining neural similarity, scene-conditioned pose priors, and observed-pose consistency. We construct a maritime scene-pose library and model the pose and scale priors nonparametrically, as a kernel that conditions each prior continuously on the scene with no learned parameters. Across seven maritime benchmarks, our trained scene-conditioned retriever exceeds the strongest appearance encoder (SigLIP 2) in recall (+0.14), and the training-free prior raises geometric plausibility further at negligible recall cost, more than halving the constraint violations of appearance retrieval and outperforming learned foreground-search baselines (GALA-style, DiscoFOS). In a blind study of end-to-end composites (BootPlace placement, DiffHarmony harmonization), SEALECT ranks first among six methods, ahead of random and GALA-style selection and statistically tied with CLIP, DiscoFOS, and DINO.

title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
abstract: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem. When the stop is bounded subanalytic singular isotropic, we prove a Morita equivalence between the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category and a microlocal sheaf category.

title: Sharp upper and lower bounds on the variance of U-statistics
abstract: For a U-statistic with a symmetric kernel of any rank, we offer new upper and lower bounds on its variance, which are uniformly sharper than those established in the classical paper by Hoeffding (1948, Theorem 5.2). Our new bounds have strong optimality properties and can tightly describe how the variance scales with the degree of the kernel. As an application, we leverage our new upper bound to improve an existing Berry-Esseen theorem for the normal approximation of incomplete U-statistics based on Bernoulli sampling, in a computationally frugal regime where the computational budget is much smaller than the available sample size.

title: Spherically-symmetric solutions with internal Ricci-flat spaces in Brans-Dicke theory
abstract: We construct a new family of exact spherically symmetric solutions in $D$-dimensional Brans-Dicke theory with $n$ internal Ricci-flat spaces. The spacetime is assumed to be a product of a four-dimensional spherical sector and $n$ Ricci-flat internal manifolds. By performing a conformal transformation to the Einstein frame, the problem is reduced to Einstein gravity with a minimally coupled scalar field, for which the exact solution is already known. Applying the inverse transformation to the Jordan frame yields explicit expressions for the metric and the Brans-Dicke scalar field, together with a generalized algebraic constraint on the exponents. The obtained solutions generalize the four-dimensional Brans solutions and the multidimensional solutions with Ricci-flat internal spaces. We analyze the causal structure of the four-dimensional section and derive the necessary condition for the surface $R=L$ to be an event horizon, $ν\equiv \left|a+b+\frac12\sum_i a_iN_i\right| \ge 1$. A Kretschmann-scalar analysis shows that, apart from the Schwarzschild limit and the case of frozen internal spaces, a regular horizon is generically absent when the extra dimensions are dynamical. For the four-dimensional section we also obtain the photon-sphere and ISCO radii and discuss their Schwarzschild limits. The results clarify the role of nonminimal Brans-Dicke coupling in multidimensional black-hole geometries with Ricci-flat internal factors.

title: Phase-wise MLLM Tuning for Multi-framework WebUI Code Generation
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance in translating WebUI screenshots into HTML/CSS. However, when they faced multiple frameworks (React/Vue/Angular), they often suffer from negative transfer that leads to compilation failures. These failures commonly stem from mixing framework specific syntax and violating framework constraints. This paper studies supervised fine-tuning for multi-framework WebUI code generation and proposes a phase-wise MLLM tuning method driven by compatibility and heterogeneity signals across frameworks. We first apply a normalization mapping that preserves each framework's native syntax while suppressing noise from variable naming and literal content. We then estimate cross framework heterogeneity and compatibility offline, and automatically derive training groups and their ordering by maximizing a phased objective. Finally, we perform phase-wise adapter tuning to reduce cross framework interference. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our proposed method improves both generation quality and compilation success rate compared with baselines.

title: Stein Criteria for Holomorphic Fibre Bundles
abstract: In this paper, we study Steinness of holomorphic fibre bundles. Over a compact Riemann surface, we prove that every holomorphic ball bundle is weakly $1$-complete and that its total space is Stein if and only if it admits no holomorphic section. We also obtain higher-dimensional Stein criteria for reductive ball bundles and affine bundles in terms of positivity of the canonical class. A topological obstruction to the $1$-convexity of holomorphic fibre bundles is also established.

title: Direct Covariance-to-Beamformer Mapping for Low-Latency Hybrid ISAC Beamforming with Subsequent DoA Estimation
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems typically employ a two-stage beamforming pipeline, in which target directions are first estimated from the received covariance matrix and then used to compute the beamforming weights by solving non-convex optimization problems. Although effective, this approach introduces processing latency that can limit beam adaptation in dynamic environments. This letter proposes a beamforming deep neural network (BFDNN) for direct covariance-to-beamformer learning in ISAC systems. BFDNN is a compact regression network that maps covariance-matrix features directly to the hybrid beamforming weights produced by a hybrid ISAC beamformer, eliminating the direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation stage during inference. Compared with MUSIC, classification-DNN, and regression-DNN based beamforming pipelines, BFDNN generates comparable beam patterns and higher effective spectral efficiencies while reducing the beamforming prediction latency by 25-30 times on the evaluated platform, demonstrating the potential of direct covariance-to-beamformer learning for low-latency ISAC beam updates. Moreover, the target directions can be inferred indirectly from the generated radiation pattern, yielding DoA accuracy competitive with that of dedicated learning-based methods in the evaluated scenario.

title: SPAR: Experience-Driven Strategy Evolution in Multi-Session B2B Sales
abstract: B2B outbound sales involves high transaction values and relationship-based trust, so closing a deal typically requires multiple rounds of outreach building on prior context. Existing LLM-based sales agents operate within single sessions and cannot carry forward context or refine strategies from experience. Methods that do learn from experience store lessons as unstructured text and treat all outcomes as equally informative, with no mechanism to distinguish a flawed strategy from an external factor. We propose SPAR, a self-evolving framework that models selling strategies as testable hypotheses and refines them without parameter updates. A double-loop architecture lets an inner loop adapt to individual merchants through episodic memory while an outer loop evolves a shared strategy playbook through causal attribution and hypothesis-driven evolution. In a live A/B test on the 1688 platform with over 200,000 merchants, SPAR achieves +15.8% conversion lift and +35.8% high-intent merchant growth. Human evaluation by domain experts rates SPAR at 4.62 out of 5 on overall sales quality, the highest among all methods.

title: Restoring Semantic Fidelity for Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation in Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based text-to-image models have recently achieved remarkable success in image synthesis. However, when directly applied beyond their training resolution, these models often suffer from severe semantic degradation, where meaningful semantic content disappears. Although existing training-free high-resolution generation methods can mitigate this issue, the inherent semantic degradation at high resolutions remains largely unresolved, leading to degraded fine-grained details. Furthermore, widely used structural guidance methods lack modeling of the structure and details in the intermediate trajectory, which degrades the quality of the generated results. In this paper, we propose a training-free framework for high-resolution image generation to address these challenges. First, we propose a text-visual scale-decoupled attention (TVSDA) module, which restores the model's ability to generate semantically meaningful content at high resolutions by preserving the global receptive field of text tokens while aligning the receptive field of image tokens with the training resolution. Second, we propose a structure-detail guidance (SDG) strategy that explicitly models structural information and fine details through scale-wise and temporal-wise guidance, overcoming the limitations of conventional low-resolution guidance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves both structural coherence and detail fidelity over existing training-free DiT-based high-resolution generation approaches. The code is available at https://github.com/ljjcoder/Restoring-Semantic-Fidelity.

title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
abstract: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $μ$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

title: Subset-system derived topologies and coreflective categories of $T_0$-spaces
abstract: Given a subset system $H$ on $T_0$-spaces, we associate with each topology a closure-testing derived topology and study the fixed points of this operator. The $H$-determined topologies above a given topology are closed under intersections and hence determine a least fixed-point hull. We prove that this hull is obtained by transfinite iteration, is functorial, and defines a right adjoint to the inclusion of $H$-determined spaces into $\mathbf{Top}_0$. Consequently, the corresponding full subcategory is coreflective and complete. We isolate restriction-stability and open-locality hypotheses under which determinedness is inherited by closed and open subspaces, and we establish a general non-reflectivity criterion. If $H$ is contained in the directed-subset system, the category of $H$-determined spaces is Cartesian closed; its exponentials are obtained by coreflecting the pointwise convergence topology on continuous maps. The construction subsumes familiar monotone- and irreducible-determined cases while separating the formal consequences of the subset-system axioms from the additional hypotheses needed for heredity and exponentials. It therefore provides a uniform categorical mechanism for producing complete Cartesian closed categories of $T_0$-spaces with explicit higher-order function spaces, as required in denotational semantics.

title: Chaotic Dynamics of Charged Particles in Magnetic Fields with Singular Forces
abstract: We study charged-particle dynamics under a non-Lipschitz velocity-dependent force with magnetic and damping effects, focusing on continuation through zero velocity and chaos in the velocity direction. For a time-independent directional force and fixed parameters, we introduce a $C^1$ regularization. When an unregularized trajectory reaches zero velocity in finite time, inner rescaling yields convergence to a reference orbit within the regularization ball, while the regularized trajectories converge locally uniformly outside it to a unique continuation. For the directional dynamics, stereographic projection yields a parameterized Euclidean system. By choosing the skew-symmetric magnetic part, we obtain a nonautonomous parameterized center manifold reduction with a prescribed finite Taylor jet. Under an additional factorization assumption, the reduced dynamics admits Shilnikov homoclinic orbits and associated chaos.

title: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
abstract: AI agents often rely on persistent memory to retain user preferences and operational rules across sessions. However, this capability introduces a new safety risk: malicious instructions from messages, documents, or Web content can be retained in memory and influence future tasks even after the original attack content is removed. Existing attack success metrics, however, fail to capture who is affected and how attacks translate into downstream harm during otherwise normal task execution. We introduce MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark for evaluating cross-session prompt injection in memory-persistent AI agents. MemHarmBench considers three categories of potential victims: users, workspace/project owners, and external stakeholders. Our evaluation first exposes an agent to malicious instructions and tests whether they are retained in memory. We then remove the attack content and initiate a new session with a legitimate task while preserving the agent's memory. We jointly evaluate whether the agent follows the attacker's intent, completes the legitimate task, and exhibits observable execution anomalies. Across multiple agent systems, we find that cross-session attacks can remain behaviorally stealthy: agents often complete tasks normally and exhibit no detectable anomalies while still making critical decisions aligned with the attacker's intent. By connecting malicious memory retention to downstream decisions and affected parties, MemHarmBench provides a systematic framework for exposing safety risks that conventional attack- and task-success metrics may overlook. We publicly release MemHarmBench at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/MemHarmBench.

title: Just-in-Time Skill Retrieval via Long-Horizon State Tracking
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external skill libraries to support complex task execution. However, determining which skills are needed remains challenging in long-horizon tasks. Existing methods typically select a fixed skill set before execution, implicitly assuming that a task's procedural requirements can be determined from its initial description. This assumption is restrictive for long-horizon interaction, where new requirements emerge from intermediate observations, execution outcomes, and newly revealed constraints. This motivates just-in-time skill retrieval, which dynamically selects skills as execution unfolds. Just-in-time skill retrieval is promising but challenging: the utility of a skill depends not only on the current context, but also on the evolving task state shaped by prior steps. To this end, we propose JitSkill, a state-grounded framework that addresses this challenge through continuous task-state tracking. By connecting emerging requirements with accumulated task progress, JitSkill provides procedural support throughout execution without treating each retrieval decision independently. Experiments across three agent benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness in improving long-horizon task completion. Our code is available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/JitSkill.git/.

title: SparseLift: Automatically Optimizing Opaque Sparse Paths in Industrial-Scale Recommendation Model Training
abstract: The sparse path, comprising sparse operations and collective communication, is a critical component of large-scale recommendation models. However, these operations are often represented as opaque nodes in the training computation graph, hindering whole-graph optimization. We present SparseLift, a low-overhead compiler for the sparse path of large-scale recommendation training. It exposes sparse computation and communication to whole-graph analysis to expand the optimization space and improve training efficiency. By analyzing model structure and runtime information, SparseLift reconstructs opaque nodes as analyzable subgraphs, recovering the resource semantics of sparse computation and communication within the graph. Building on the recovered semantics, we design incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to automatically select and organize subgraph optimizations into an execution plan that is reused during subsequent steady-state training. We evaluate SparseLift on an industrial video-platform recommendation task with 100B sparse parameters and the public DLRM benchmark. SparseLift improves steady-state throughput for ordinary industrial training steps by 16.5\% over the native baseline. On DLRM, it achieves $1.60\times$ and $1.26\times$ model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline and TorchRec, respectively.

title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.

title: MatMoE: Matryoshka Mixture-of-Experts with Dynamic Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient Inference
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture has been widely adopted in large language models (LLMs) since it reduces the computational cost through sparse expert activation. However, the massive parameter scale of MoE models hinders their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Although existing mixed-precision quantization reduces the model size, they are inherently static, fixing the bit-width of each expert across decoding steps. Such static schemes yield suboptimal performance as they overlook the dynamic variation in expert importance during decoding. Furthermore, they fail to adapt to the dynamic latency constraint driven by the fluctuating system utilization. To address these challenges, we propose MatMoE, a dynamic mixed-precision quantization framework for efficient MoE inference. MatMoE features: (1) a Matryoshka MoE PTQ algorithm that enables experts to operate flexibly at multiple precisions within a stringent memory budget; (2) a floor-and-compensation quantization method that eliminates redundant memory accesses in the Matryoshka representation; and (3) a dynamic bit-width allocation strategy that determines the precision for each expert based on their routing scores to satisfy the dynamic latency requirement. We implement our MatMoE system atop llama.cpp for both CPU and GPU platforms. Extensive evaluations across three modern MoE models and challenging benchmarks demonstrate that MatMoE achieves $4.0\% \sim 18.3\%$ higher accuracy than state-of-the-art static mixed-precision method. Compared to llama.cpp, MatMoE delivers $1.3\times \sim 3.7\times$ speedup on Raspberry Pi 5, and $1.2\times \sim 1.3\times$ speedup on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Orin.

title: Fréchet Oral Distance: A Coordinate-Free Metric and Benchmark for Speech-Driven Oral Animation
abstract: Recently, speech-driven facial and oral animation technologies have been used in various fields such as education, speech therapy, and healthcare. But methods to objectively evaluate the quality of generated results are still limited. Accordingly, we propose the Fréchet Oral Distance (FOD), which uses embeddings from an Oral Motion Encoder (OME) and a TIMIT-Vis reference distribution. In experiments, FOD reproduced model rankings similar to the coordinate-based metric, Lip Vertex Error (LVE), and showed trends consistent with user preference. Our framework provides objective and reproducible benchmarking without relying on expensive equipment or subjective evaluation, and it can be extended to compare a variety of 2D/3D models.

title: Agent-Based Disruption Simulation on an Edge-Level Product-Annotated Supply Network of the Automotive Industry
abstract: Disruptions spread through supply networks when customers cannot replace the products they lose. We ask how portfolio-overlap and product-specific rules for selecting candidate suppliers change cascades when customers search for new suppliers and form new supply edges. From the MarkLines database, we construct a product-annotated network of about 77,000 firms and 197,000 supplier-customer edges in the global automotive industry. We extend an agent-based disruption model with edge-level products, a product-specific substitution rule based on the semantic similarity of product names, and calibrated capacities and inventories. Only 6% of the edges carry observed products. We impute the others and test the imputation against the annotated edges. We run 119,000 simulations. With all other mechanics fixed, the product-specific rule makes the cascades after a hub failure four to five times larger than the portfolio-overlap rule of the original model. Under alternative imputations and similarity thresholds, the factor ranges from 1.2 to 18. Within the simulations, substitutability also shapes which suppliers are critical. Network topology largely determines which firms a shock reaches, and substitutability determines how many of them fail. Of the 50 most damaging suppliers under random disruptions, topology alone identifies 20 and an index that adds product substitutability identifies 32. The index carries over without refitting to a regional scenario modelled on the 2011 Tohoku Earthquake. Supply network risk assessment should account for product-level substitutability and therefore needs product data on supply relationships.

title: SMART-AIMC: Sensitivity-Aware Mixed ADC Resolution with Fine-Grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing
abstract: Analog In-Memory Computing (IMC) is a promising paradigm for accelerating GEMM-based AI workloads by executing computations directly within the memory array in the analog domain. While IMC delivers substantial energy and throughput improvements, it can suffer from significant task accuracy degradation due to analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization noise, which occurs at the GEMM output and is thus different from weight/activation quantization, which occurs at the GEMM input. Mixed ADC resolution allows IMC modules to choose between high- and low-resolution ADC modes with different energy costs, offering a compelling accuracy-energy trade-off. However, selecting ADC resolutions across IMC units while respecting hardware granularity constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose SMART-AIMC, a Sensitivity-aware Mixed ADC Resolution framework with fine-grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing. SMART-AIMC correlates the algorithmic task loss to hardware ADC quantization noise in the form of an ADC Channel Sensitivity (ACS) metric. Using this metric, SMART-AIMC systematically, and in a disciplined manner, allocates ADC resources to critical computations. Furthermore, we introduce a sensitivity-based channel reordering scheme that overcomes the hardware granularity constraints with no runtime overhead and approaches the optimal ADC quantization possible for the model. Evaluated across diverse workloads, SMART-AIMC unlocks a superior accuracy-energy Pareto frontier, providing (1) higher task accuracy at matched energy budgets and (2) fine-grained tuning across efficiency targets, from aggressive energy savings to near-digital inference accuracy. At the latter operating point, SMART-AIMC achieves $6.99\times$ higher modeled system-level energy efficiency for linear projections than the INT8 digital baseline with negligible accuracy degradation.

title: A new upper bound for the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$
abstract: Fauzan's determinantal proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational also yields $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-260}$ for all large $b$. The exponent is the product $\varrhoλ/\varepsilon$ of three constants attached to the construction, of which $\varrho$ governs the growth of a relative matrix norm. We show that $\varrho$ may be taken to be $9.09$ instead of $6933/500=13.866$, and deduce $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-171}$ for all integers $a$ and all sufficiently large integers $b$, so that the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$ is at most $171$. Two closed-form functions replace two worst-case estimates: a node function, which bounds the residue weights individually instead of uniformly, and the external field of the energy estimate, which replaces a factor-by-factor bound on the weight. The result is conditional on Fauzan's preprint. An exact arithmetic verifier is attached.

title: Comparative Strategies for Handling Imbalanced QSAR Regression: A Case Study on hERG Activity Prediction
abstract: Data imbalance frequently occurs in QSAR modeling, yet most studies focus on classification tasks, and few address regression tasks, as it is challenging to determine which regions of the data are sparse or dense. Data-level and algorithm-level imbalance-handling strategies can have different effects on model performance. In this study, we systematically compare various strategies across GCN and fingerprint-based machine learning models. To evaluate model performance more meaningfully, we partitioned the target region into several subregions based on both domain knowledge and data distribution. We focused on the region of greatest practical interest. Our results demonstrate that selecting models based on this interest-region metric leads to more reliable performance than using the total region metric. We also observed that different imbalance-handling strategies can have divergent effects depending on the model type. These findings highlight the importance of region-aware evaluation in regression QSAR modeling and provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate strategies for imbalanced datasets.

title: CST: Lightweight Risk Triage with Source-Grounded Evidence for Web Discussions
abstract: Web communities rely on moderators to catch harmful messages such as insults, hate speech, and scams, but no one can read every message. Existing tools give each message a risk score, which tells moderators where to look but not what to read or how to check it. Yet meaning depends on context: the same reply, "I agree.", can support or oppose removing someone from a group. Moderators therefore need source-grounded evidence, not just scores: a few key messages kept with their original wording and replies. We present CST, a lightweight triage pipeline that first decides where to look, then what to show. It scores risk by pairing character patterns, which capture exact wording, with sentence meaning from a fixed multilingual model, so it handles several languages and runs on an ordinary CPU. It then groups related messages and picks from each group in turn, so a small reading budget covers different parts of a discussion, and links every pick back to the original thread. Across six tasks from five datasets in several languages, CST ranks harmful messages more accurately than a fully fine-tuned multilingual model and, under the same budget, finds more of them than reading by score alone. In a user study, reviewers needed at least 27% less time with CST's grouped evidence while keeping decision accuracy above 94%. CST turns risk scores into evidence that moderators can read quickly and check in context. Code and dataset reconstruction resources will be released at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/CST-MIL.

title: Irrationality measures for $Γ(1/4)$ and $Γ(1/3)$
abstract: Let $μ$ denote the irrationality exponent. Bruiltet proved in 2002 that $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 10^{143}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 10^{151}$. We prove $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 3.24\cdot 10^{26}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 1.74\cdot 10^{26}$, with explicit thresholds $h(p/q)\ge 5.4\cdot 10^{7}$ and $h(p/q)\ge 4.7\cdot 10^{7}$ respectively, against $10^{75}$ and $10^{79}$ in the published statements. The proof keeps the architecture of Bruiltet's argument -- Philippon's transcendence criterion together with a zero estimate in commutative algebraic groups -- and replaces three of its ingredients. First, an approximate Schwarz principle based on Hermite interpolation replaces the gravitation estimate of Reyssat; on a lattice point set its cost per node is governed by a lattice energy and drops from about 3.7 to about 1.0. Second, a summation lemma for the failure of Diaz's approximation lemma sharpens the passage from an approximation measure to an irrationality measure. Third, the auxiliary point is taken at a torsion point of order 4, respectively 3, which lowers the degree of the base field from 8d to 2d. All numerical constants are produced by a verifier run in interval arithmetic, supplied as ancillary files.

title: When Disagreement Labels Do Not Identify F1 Rankings
abstract: Agreement labels cancel from an accuracy comparison but can change an F1 ranking. We specialize partial identification to an explicit audit after labeling disagreements: two agreement counts give exact bounds, certifying a ranking or a choice within a specified F1 tolerance under every completion. Across 3,200 frozen model pairs, shared completions tighten bounds and a 0.01 tolerance reduces labeling costs. A zero-loss (weak-winner) control attributes most savings to positive tolerance, not ties. Guarantees concern the evaluated batch, not future data.

title: Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair for Safe Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can generate task-oriented robot actions, but they do not guarantee safe execution in obstacle-rich manipulation scenes. Although CBF-QP safety filters can locally project unsafe actions into a safe set, such correction may push the robot away from the learned task trajectory and leave the VLA policy without a reliable recovery direction. We propose Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair, a post-hoc repair module that uses the short-horizon action chunk predicted by the VLA to detect blocked nominal trajectories and generate entry-exit-rejoin guidance around obstacles. The selected route is added to the CBF-QP objective as a soft guidance term, while the CBF safety constraint remains hard. On SafeLIBERO, our method improves collision avoidance, task success, and SafeSuccess compared with AEGIS. Our project page is available at GitHub.

title: The Three-Color Generalized Schur Number of \(x+(k-1)y=z\): A Proof for All \(k\) from a Critical Set of 33 Polynomials
abstract: For an integer \(k\ge 3\), let \(T_k(3)\) be the least positive integer \(N\) such that, for any \(3\)-coloring of \([1,N]\), there exists a monochromatic solution to \(x+(k-1)y=z\). In this paper, we prove that \(T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2\) for all \(k\ge 3\). In the notation \(s_a(3)\) of the first author, with \(a=k-1\), this says that \(s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1\) for all \(a\ge 2\), which confirms the conjecture proposed in 2020. Note that every solution to \(x+(k-1)y=z\) is also a solution to \(x_1+\dots+x_k=x_{k+1}\). So the theorem also gives a new proof of the upper bound in the three-color theorem of Boza, Marín, Revuelta and Sanz, using only this restricted equation. The lower bound is an explicit recursive coloring. For the upper bound, we fix one set \(\Xmin\) of \(33\) polynomials in \(k\), together with the \(144\) polynomial identities \(z=x+(k-1)y\) that hold among them, and we show that no \(3\)-coloring of \(\Xmin\) avoids a monochromatic identity. Since every relation is an identity in \(k\), a single argument covers all \(k\). The argument is a case analysis with \(62\) cases and depth \(8\), and it uses only two elementary rules. It is written out in full in an appendix and has been checked by an independent program. The set \(\Xmin\) is critical, that is, removing any one of its elements makes it \(3\)-colorable. It is also a critical subset of minimum size of the \(51\)-element set from which it was extracted. Finally, we describe the rigid structure shared by all extremal colorings of \([1,k^3+2k^2-3]\).

title: EarlySelectKV: Anticipatory KV Selection via Cross-Layer Query Proxies
abstract: Query-conditioned sparse KV selection reduces long-context inference cost by attending to a subset of historical KV entries at each decoding step. Existing selectors must wait for the target-layer query before scoring candidates and generating indices, placing routing on the immediate pre-attention path. We introduce EarlySelectKV, a training-free transformation that uses proxy queries from earlier hidden states to precompute selected KV indices while retaining the real target-layer query for final attention. Tests with RocketKV, Quest, and Loki show no consistent pattern of quality degradation across the evaluated settings. In the primary RocketKV evaluation, ES-RocketKV differs by +0.018 points on LongBench, approximately -0.01 points on RULER, and +0.25 percentage points on representative NIAH/Passkey settings. In a TensorRT-LLM deployment with CPU-offloaded routing, ES-RocketKV improves end-to-end output throughput by up to 12.4% and reduces GPU-resident memory by 11.1% of the combined KV/K-summary pool. This makes routing timing an explicit optimization target alongside KV subset selection in sparse long-context decoding. Code is available at https://github.com/sea-with-sakura/EarlySelectKV.

title: Derived Torelli for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds
abstract: We prove that every orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between the integral Mukai lattices of the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds is induced by an exact equivalence. The proof uses Markman--Mehrotra's comonad reconstruction method to recover both Kuznetsov components from a common Fourier--Mukai comonad on a moduli space of stable objects. As an application, we prove that the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds are equivalent whenever their Fano varieties of lines are derived equivalent.

title: Algebraic properties of Toeplitz operators on annulus and multiply connected domains
abstract: We study the Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over the annulus and provide a complete characterization of them. Based on that, we single out a certain class of Toeplitz operators that satisfy the multiplicativity property and lead to a zero product theorem. We further extend the results for the general multiply-connected domain and prove the zero product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over such a domain.

title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
abstract: Task success, retrieval quality, and cost do not show whether an LLM agent used a delivered memory or what followed from that use. We introduce MemUse, which evaluates memory at its point of use in recorded trajectories: each memory delivery is compared with what the agent could already see and followed through the agent's later actions and their consequences. An agentic judge rates each delivered entry's relevance, accuracy, novelty, influence, and observed effect; programmatic checks enforce complete reading of cited evidence, and fixed rules aggregate the ratings into verdicts linked to memory histories and delivery cost. On 8,000 SWE-bench Verified episodes from three memory systems, resolve rates stay within 0.4 percentage points of a no-memory baseline, yet MemUse shows that most delivered entries were irrelevant, most relevant entries went unused, and in two systems most deliveries restated content the agent could still see. It also surfaces effects that outcomes hide: 23.2\% of episodes with beneficial memory use still failed, and 5 of 16 with harmful use still succeeded.

title: Strict Separation of Antiperiodic Degeneracy Curves for Elliptic Euler and Lagrangian Solutions
abstract: We prove strict separation of antiperiodic degeneracy curves associated with elliptic Euler and Lagrangian solutions of the planar three-body problem. For every eccentricity $0<e<1$, each Euler pair issuing from a common circular parameter is strictly ordered in the extended family $β>0$, and the two Lagrangian curves remain disjoint. Every antiperiodic degeneracy point in these families with $0<e<1$ has a one-dimensional full kernel. Rotation and reflection decomposition yield, for each model, two half-integer Fourier block operators with identical tails and different first blocks. In the Euler case, a positive definite first-block perturbation gives a definite connecting crossing form; a spectral-flow rectangle and sectorwise index counts then force strict separation. In the Lagrangian case, exact tail elimination and an explicit estimate for a two-dimensional Schur complement exclude simultaneous degeneracy in the two reflection sectors.

title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. To produce the radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed to be most likely an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of $-(6.8-9.6)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$ when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD ($1.4~M_\odot$). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than $1.4~M_\odot$ if the measured period derivative exceeds $-9.6\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra-contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a $1.0-1.6~M_\odot$ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of $-(4.9-13.5)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of $1.35-1.5~M_\odot$. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be $0.006$ when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

title: GDBack: A Group-Delay Backdoor Attack on Speaker Identification via Analytic All-Pass Filtering
abstract: Existing phase-based backdoor attacks on speaker identification rely on shared absolute phase patterns for cross-sample trigger consistency, while other audio backdoor attacks have explored shared transformations that produce input-dependent triggers. Whether phase-based triggers can achieve similar consistency without imposing identical output phase patterns remains unclear. We propose GDBack, a poison-only group-delay backdoor attack using cascaded second-order analytic all-pass filters. Applying a shared transformation across utterances ideally preserves spectral magnitude while introducing a consistent frequency-dependent phase response and group-delay contribution, without forcing identical output phases. Experiments on LibriSpeech and VoxCeleb1 with ECAPA-TDNN, x-vector, and RawNet3 achieve attack success rates above 94% across all six settings (97.00% on average), while maintaining benign accuracy close to clean models. Phase and magnitude interventions, inverse compensation, and parameter-sensitivity analyses support the role of the induced phase transformation in backdoor activation. Speech quality and content evaluations indicate limited perceptual and linguistic distortion, while robustness experiments, including real over-the-air tests, reveal varying effectiveness across conditions and architectures. These findings demonstrate that cross-sample trigger consistency can arise from a shared phase transformation without requiring a common absolute phase pattern.

title: Higher-Order Symmetry Energy Effects on the Properties of Neutron Stars
abstract: We study the effects of the symmetry-energy curvature $K_{\rm sym}$ on the equation of state (EoS) and neutron-star properties within the relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework. We construct controlled families of RMF parametrizations based on the TM1 and IUFSU models by varying $K_{\rm sym}$ while keeping the symmetry energy $J$ and its slope $L$ fixed at saturation density. We find that, although a larger $K_{\rm sym}$ leads to a lower symmetry energy at suprasaturation densities and a reduced proton fraction in $β$-equilibrated matter, it results in a stiffer EoS and a higher sound speed. The maximum neutron-star mass is weakly affected, whereas the canonical radius $R_{1.4}$ exhibits a nearly linear dependence on $K_{\rm sym}$.

title: A sensor-driven physics-informed neural network for real-time occupant-centric space heating control
abstract: Conventional space heating systems typically rely on single or sparse fixed-point temperature measurements, overlooking non-uniform indoor temperature distributions, transient thermal dynamics, and occupant-specific comfort requirements. This study explores an occupant-centric control strategy that aims to maintain the desired temperature around the occupant location. Spatially and temporally varying temperature fields, together with occupant mobility, make real-time local temperature estimation challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a control-oriented Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model for indoor temperature-field prediction. Conventional PINNs rely on explicit time inputs and assume consistent temporal patterns across samples, which limits adaptability under variable initial conditions and heating sequences. The proposed model infers temporal dynamics implicitly from spatial coordinates and limited sensor measurements, improving robustness to changes in initial conditions and external disturbances. The method was validated across nine horizontal sensing planes in three controlled room-scale configurations. Against a validated COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, the PINN predicted the evaluated temperature fields with a maximum relative error below 1.85% across validation cases. These predictions supported an occupant-centric space heating control scheme. Compared with COMSOL-based offline control, the PINN-based system achieved an average prediction error of around 0.67%, and its rapid inference supports real-time occupant-centric control implementation. This work represents a move away from reliance on fixed-point temperature measurements in space heating control to an occupant-centric control strategy informed by real-time environmental feedback.

title: Beyond Imputation: Mask-Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Tree Embeddings on General Missing Data Mechanisms
abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free framework for uncertainty quantification with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. Yet, missing values introduce distributional heterogeneity, where marginal coverage can hide systematic undercoverage for certain missingness patterns. At the same time, existing methods based on distances or smoothness require a continuous representation of partially observed covariates. Although imputation restores continuity, it obscures the missingness patterns and introduces task-dependent overhead. We develop a new CP framework that is \emph{adaptive to missingness patterns}, without imputing covariates. We rely on data augmentation by feature embedding that accounts for missingness. Our framework represents each input with missing values by a tree embedding together with its raw missingness mask, and then learns a regularized quantile score function. Varying the choices for the penalty function and the augmentation enables us to characterize three practically relevant validity levels: exact coordinate-wise validity, exact validity on observed masks, and approximate missingness-conditional guarantees for general mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support these guarantees and show that the proposed method reduces miscoverage risk while maintaining informative intervals, especially in non-MCAR settings. These results highlight the practical value of uncertainty quantification that adapts to missingness.

title: Uniqueness of SRB measures for stochastic differential equations
