abstract: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi$_2$Se$_3$ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated $J_1$--$J_2$ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the Néel structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.22$, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. Band inversion of the renormalized tight-binding model occurs on the same critical locus, producing jumps in the Chern number and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant mirrored by the skyrmion charge $Q$. This gives a microscopic link: $Q$ selects the axion angle and thus the topological magnetoelectric coupling. We distinguish axion coupling, independent of skyrmion helicity, from the helicity-dependent magnetoelectric multipole coupling, whose toroidal component scales as $\sinγ$ and vanishes for Néel-type textures. We derive the $Q$-topological magnetoelectric energy and estimate $\sim 10^{-20}\,\mathrm{J}$ per skyrmion per cycle for few-tesla fields. The cycle is thermodynamically bounded: constant-$θ$ cycles extract no net work, and efficiency is limited by axionic entropy change.

title: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation
abstract: An important physical quantity that is part of the Saha ionisation equation is the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. An immense uncertainty is caused by the divergency of the neutral atom partition function arising due to the fast growing degeneracy factor of its excited n-state. We suggested a regularisation and renormalisation procedure for the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. The renormalised partition function is well defined and allows to calculate the population of the energy levels and the ionisation state of the hydrogen plasma as a function of its temperature and pressure. In the low-temperature limit the behaviour of these functions smoothly transforms to the Saha equation, which is used in the description of the low-temperature plasma. At higher temperatures the renormalised ionisation equation describes the deviation from the Saha equation. The application of the renormalised ionisation equation to the solar core and atmosphere is considered.

title: Long-horizon Forecasting of Sodium-ion Battery Charge-profile Evolution and Degradation using Autoregressive Deep Sequence Models
abstract: Accurate long-horizon battery ageing prediction remains challenging because degradation alters not only scalar health indicators but also the shape and duration of electrochemical cycling profiles. Here, we introduce an autoregressive deep sequence-learning framework to forecast voltage-current profiles and state-of-health (SOH) evolution in NVPF/hard-carbon sodium-ion batteries. Stacked LSTM (Batt-LSTM) and hybrid CNN-LSTM (Batt-LSTM-C) models learn from voltage, current, and cycle-index sequences to generate future cycling profiles iteratively from measured data. Scheduled sampling mitigates the training-inference mismatch during autoregressive rollout, extending stable forecasting horizons from a few tens of cycles to as many as 600 cycles while preserving local waveform fidelity. Horizon-dependent benchmarking against classical machine-learning models evaluates voltage mean absolute error (MAE), global and local dynamic time warping (DTW), and SOH MAE across five forecasting horizons. Batt-LSTM with scheduled sampling achieves the lowest voltage MAE at horizons from 5,000 to 20,000 time steps. The predicted profiles also enable extraction of capacity-, resistance-, and energy-based SOH indicators, together with internal-resistance evolution. Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles estimate predictive spread at local profile and global degradation-trajectory scales. Fine-tuning on an independent ageing dataset improves cross-cell adaptation, with rolling-horizon updates reducing SOH prediction error to 3.844 percentage points for a 200-cycle horizon. These results show that curve-level forecasting retains diagnostically relevant electrochemical information beyond scalar SOH regression and offers a route toward uncertainty-aware, adaptive battery-health monitoring.

title: A Simulation-Driven Digital Workflow Integrating Bayesian Optimization for Early-Stage Process Design: A Methyl Acetate Production Case Study
abstract: Methyl acetate production via direct carbonylation of dimethyl ether and carbon monoxide involves strong nonlinear interactions among reactor operation, recycle structure, and energy consumption, making conventional simulation-based optimization computationally demanding. In this work, a data-driven framework integrating steady-state process simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization was developed for process intensification. A dataset of 2730 steady-state simulations was generated using a Python-based automated process simulation workflow and a structured design of experiments across the operating domain. Surrogate models were trained to predict carbon conversion yield (C-yield) and cost of specific energy consumption (C-SEC), with neural network-based models showing the best predictive performance and robustness. These models were integrated into a multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework to identify optimal operating regions. Results indicate that high C-yield (up to ~95%) can be achieved with reduced energy cost through lower recycle flow rates and compression demand. Pareto analysis revealed a nonlinear trade-off between C-yield and C-SEC, where further improvements near the conversion limit require disproportionately higher energy input. Validation against rigorous simulations showed deviations below 3% for C-yield and 10% for C-SEC.

title: ReVi: Recursive Recap Video Generation
abstract: Novels tell rich stories, but their textual form cannot directly present the sights and sounds of the worlds they describe. Film adaptations offer an audiovisual experience but require substantial production effort and viewing time; film recaps are shorter but depend on existing footage. Neither route directly provides a concise audiovisual account of a novel. We therefore study novel-to-recap video generation: producing a self-contained, source-grounded audiovisual retelling directly from a novel within a fixed viewing-time budget. This task requires compressing the story while preserving causal connections, allocating sufficient time to retained events, and aligning narration with newly generated visuals. We propose ReVi, a dual-loop multi-agent framework guided by edit first, generate second. Its Inner Loop plans story content, narration time, and corresponding shots before video generation. Across novels, its Outer Loop performs recursive self-improvement by revising both the editing policy and the meta policy that governs its revision. Experiments on two evaluation sets show that ReVi improves recap quality and duration compliance over representative baselines, with human ratings and multi-round improvement results providing further support.

title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. Their symmetric nature cannot capture directional processes, such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible (e.g. tumor growth dynamics or cognitive improvement in Alzheimer's disease). Although Riemannian metrics extend Euclidean geometry by incorporating curvature, they remain symmetric. We show that understanding asymmetry and not curvature alone directly addresses these problems. To do so we propose a new Finsler-Randers metric learning framework. It incorporates direction-dependent distances, thus enabling the computation of trajectories respecting monotonic sequential constraints. We demonstrate its potential for interpolation and extrapolation on controlled cross-sectional datasets.

title: A local orchestration harness for molecular design with foundation models
abstract: Molecular design requires coordinated generation, property prediction and iterative editing, with each decision linked to the correct chemical structure and supporting evidence. Integrating these capabilities in practice presents three major challenges: retaining local control of molecular data, connecting specialized models across tasks and verifying that proposed changes satisfy chemical constraints. Here we present MolCrew, a locally deployable system that coordinates four separately trained molecular specialists with a language-model orchestrator and RDKit calculations. The specialists generate structures from descriptions, describe molecular structures, predict biological endpoints and propose edits towards specified goals. Separate model weights allow each capability to be evaluated and updated independently within the workflow. RDKit calculations check structural validity, quantify descriptor changes and assess specified structural constraints, while returned observations guide further tool calls. We evaluated low-rank adaptation of the orchestrator for tool-use decisions and failure recovery while leaving specialist weights unchanged. On 3,300 ChEBI-20 test examples, MolCrew achieved 96.4% exact structure recovery, compared with 38.7% for published Atomas-large results. Across eight MoleculeNet datasets evaluated using scaffold splits, mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.851, compared with 0.770 for published Atomas results. In a recorded evaluation using the unadapted orchestrator, 1,554 of 1,699 requests (91.5%) passed every predefined workflow check. By preserving inspectable links between molecular proposals, model outputs and chemical calculations, MolCrew provides a modular framework for computational candidate assessment and refinement under local data control.

title: A Pair-Weighted Reciprocal-Cost Representation of the von Weizsäcker Functional
abstract: We investigate pair-weighted lattice energies constructed from the reciprocal ratio cost $J(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+x^{-1})-1$ and their connection to the von Weizsäcker kinetic-energy functional. When the pair weight depends only on the common multiplicative amplitude scale and is quadratic under uniform amplitude rescaling, it takes the form $B(u,v)=Cuv$. For the normalization $C=1$, the weighted edge cost reduces exactly to $\frac{1}{2}(u-v)^2$ for arbitrary positive neighboring amplitudes, without requiring a small-deviation expansion. On a Cartesian lattice, the resulting discrete energy converges to $\frac{1}{2}\int |\nabla u|^2,d\mathbf r$, with leading correction $-\frac{h^2}{24}\sum_k\int(\partial_k^2u)^2,d\mathbf r+O(h^4)$ under the stated regularity conditions. Identifying $u=\sqrtρ$ and restoring the factor $\hbar^2/m$ yields the von Weizsäcker functional. By contrast, the unweighted ratio cost approaches a scale-invariant log-Dirichlet action and does not have kinetic-energy dimensions. Numerical benchmarks confirm the expected lattice convergence and assess the discretization error in smooth, nodal, cusp, and molecular cases. For $\mathrm{H}_2^+$ densities obtained from aug-cc-pV5Z orbitals, a four-grid least-squares $h^2+h^4$ extrapolation agrees with orbital kinetic energies within $1.5\times10^{-4}$ relative over $R=1$--$6,a_0$. Alternative extrapolations indicate a conservative sensitivity of up to approximately $5\times10^{-4}$. The construction therefore provides a conditional exact discrete representation of the von Weizsäcker sector rather than an approximation to the complete noninteracting kinetic functional.

title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configuration-independent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the long-wavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95-99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27-41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au2/MgO(001), MACE-FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5 meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel, as learned by FNOs, becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium.

title: Conformer diversity over quantity in COSMO-RS-based LLE predictions
abstract: Accurate prediction of phase equilibria is essential for chemical process design, particularly in systems characterized by complex intermolecular interactions. This work investigates the influence of conformer selection and sigma-profile characteristics on COSMO-RS predictions of liquid-liquid equilibria (LLE), using the tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA)-methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK)-water system as a case study. Calculations were performed at the TZVP and TZVPD-FINE levels of theory. While TZVP failed to capture the experimentally observed phase behavior, TZVPD-FINE provided substantially improved predictions. The differences are attributed to the relative importance assigned to less-polar conformers and more-polar conformers capable of hydrogen bonding. Although the TZVPD-FINE calculations reproduced the main experimental trends, the predicted organic-phase composition showed a mean percentage deviation of 5.27%, slightly exceeding the adopted 5% agreement threshold. Investigations using individual conformers demonstrated that predictions can be strongly influenced by conformer selection and that representative conformer ensembles are necessary for reliable results. Further analysis showed that diversity in sigma profiles is more important for predictive accuracy than the total number of conformers. These findings emphasize the importance of carefully selecting conformers when applying COSMO-RS to liquid-liquid equilibria involving phases of contrasting polarity.

title: Many Electrons, One Determinant: Hartree--Fock Theory, Basis Sets, and Molecular Integrals
abstract: This chapter accompanies the lectures on Hartree--Fock theory and on basis sets and molecular integrals at the \href{https://www.esqc.org}{European Summer School of Quantum Chemistry (ESQC) 2026}. Intended for doctoral students, it develops the single-determinant description of electronic structure from antisymmetry and the variational principle to the orbital equations and their finite-basis matrix representation. Detailed derivations connect the energy functional, the Fock operator, excited determinants, and the interpretation of orbital energies. Restricted, unrestricted, and generalized formulations show how the choice of variational space affects spin symmetry, symmetry breaking, and the limitations of the Hartree--Fock approximation. The computational development covers orthogonalization, self-consistent-field iteration, convergence acceleration, overlap-based occupation selection, and orbital analysis, distinguishing orbital stationarity from stability. A connection to second-order Møller--Plesset perturbation theory explains the correlation-energy expression and the cost of transforming electron-repulsion integrals from atomic to molecular orbitals. The basis-set and integral development examines radial and angular flexibility, contraction, basis-set incompleteness, and superposition error. The Gaussian product theorem leads to one- and two-electron integrals, recurrence relations, integral screening, and low-rank representations. Worked examples and exercises with detailed solutions connect these derivations to practical calculations. Historical perspectives and explicit notation conventions provide context for the approximations and algorithms that underpin molecular electronic-structure theory.

title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every bijective non-contractive self-map has the following structure: the quasi-metric splits as $d = λ^- + D_0$. The invariant limit register $λ^-$ is a quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which the map is an isometry, with totally bounded symmetrization on every orbit, so that the map's rigid shadow is a rotation of a compact monothetic group; the asymmetric limit structure on it, a priori only paratopological, carries the compact topology. The defect $D_0$ lies in a band between a past fee difference and the fee of its source, the fee nondecreasing along orbits and vanishing in the deep past. The defect is zero precisely when the map is an isometry. Deep sources are thus almost rigid: in the deep past the map is an isometry to within any $\varepsilon$, against every target. Every such map that is not an isometry is a toll over its rigid shadow, levied on a forward-invariant zone that sheds into the past. Two further facts are forced: the orbit of the source of any strict pair is infinite and already strict, and the source pays its whole defect on its own backward returns, uniformly on a chain-closed set of displacements. The band is attained at both ends, and beyond it the shape of the defect is not forced: three spirals over the circle show that the toll can depend on the target, that a source carrying a fee can descend for free, and that an ascent can carry defect; no rate of shedding is forced either, and for zone tolls (two-valued descent tolls that are shift-monotone and subadditive along their own routes) the fee reaches zero already at a finite depth, by the ascending chain condition on submonoids of $\mathbb{N}$. The results are machine-checked in Lean, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
abstract: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of degree 11178 on 8386560 vertices. The codes and lines were found by local search, and all configurations were checked pair by pair in exact integer arithmetic.

title: Geometry, Topology, and Confined Spectra Around Anisotropic Cosmic Strings
abstract: We study scalar, Dirac, and electromagnetic test fields on a two-parameter family of static spacetimes, labeled by an angular winding number $k$ and an anisotropy parameter $α$ that shortens one direction of the transverse metric relative to the other. Only the members with $k=1$ and $α<1$ are conical, as for an ordinary straight cosmic string. The remaining members are nonconical and, except in the flat cases, curved and nonvacuum. A common spin-weighted connection Laplacian organizes the local equations, while the curvature coupling, global field conditions, and constraints are fixed separately for each physical field. Explicit frame transitions remove spurious winding dependence in the flat limit. For the nonconical members of the family, isothermal coordinates yield an exact factorization of the indicial equation and determine its monodromy: the indicial exponents are independent of the anisotropy parameter, although the finite-domain eigenvalues are not. We derive variational bounds and a weak-anisotropy selection rule for the scalar spectrum. The electromagnetic equations are obtained from the four-potential in Lorenz gauge, with gauge-invariant transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) reductions and an annular transverse-electromagnetic (TEM) mode. Finite-element computations on an annulus, validated against benchmarks, are consistent with the bounds, confirm the selection rule, give MIT bag Dirac and conducting-wall Maxwell spectra, and reproduce the invariance of the transverse-electromagnetic capacity under $k\mapsto2-k$, an exact consequence of a radial inversion of the Dirichlet energy.

title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
abstract: Language models serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as ``The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is'', a small general-purpose model may answer ``the alkyne group'' instead of an alkyl fluoride. The output alone cannot tell whether the model failed to recognize the fluorine or recognized it and failed to say so. We address this by reading the internal representations of five open-source models on prompts covering 92 molecules and 20 functional groups. Even without chemistry training, the models organize functional groups by chemical family, and they encode chemical differences as consistent directions. The shift from thioether ($\mathrm{R{-}S{-}R'}$) to thiol ($\mathrm{R{-}SH}$), added to ether ($\mathrm{R{-}O{-}R'}$), lands nearest alcohol ($\mathrm{R{-}OH}$). This structure emerges abruptly in the middle layers, where representations shift from tracking the wording of the prompt to tracking the functional group. The base model names the correct functional group in only 58.5\% of prompts, the lowest of the five, yet it encodes functional-group families and preserves chemically meaningful patterns. Its errors are mostly failures to answer rather than wrong answers. Functional-group knowledge is structured in the model before it is spoken. Chemistry fine-tuning reorganizes it, making functional groups rather than prompt wording dominate the representation. These results suggest that evaluating chemical language models through outputs alone can underestimate the chemical information they encode. Representation analysis can distinguish a lack of knowledge from a failure to express it, which matters when choosing or adapting models for chemical agents.

title: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends
abstract: Visual agents need to coordinate reasoning and action while their environment evolves during inference. We introduce LOLPlay, a benchmark in native \emph{League of Legends} with 36 champion-specific tasks spanning resource management, combat, cooperation, and objectives. Agents interact through screenshots and mouse--keyboard actions; automated initialization and 82 executable subgoal checks distinguish partial progress from completion. Across 324 task evaluations of three models at three reasoning-effort settings, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate of 25.0\% at low and medium effort, and the highest subgoal success rate of 40.3\% at medium effort. However, high effort improves neither metric over low effort for any model. For Astra, longer requests leave fewer interaction rounds, suggesting a cost to additional reasoning in real-time control. Trajectories reveal incomplete subgoal composition and actions executing after the observed scene changes, motivating agents that combine visual reasoning with timely action.

title: Charge-Dependent Coordination and Redox Energetics of Actinide Fluoride Complexes in Molten Salts
abstract: Redox control in molten fluoride salt reactors determines actinide solubility and corrosion of structural alloys, but the role of local fluoride coordination in this control remains poorly understood. We use density functional theory with explicit LiF microsolvation to study the coordination chemistry, intrinsic redox energetics, and fluoride-exchange kinetics of Th(IV), U(IV), and U(III) fluoride complexes. The coordination response to solvation primarily follows the formal charge of the complex rather than the actinide at its center: we find that cationic and neutral complexes gain fluoride ligands, most anionic complexes keep their coordination number, and $4-$ complexes lose fluoride. Coordination number then strongly controls the intrinsic U(IV)/U(III) reduction energy. From CN 4 to CN 7, this energy rises by up to $11$ eV and changes sign; a continuum-solvation estimate opposes this trend and therefore establishes the intrinsic value as an upper bound. Fluoride exchange barriers are low, so redox partners of different charge do not keep the same coordination numbers in solvated clusters. Finally, above a threshold between CN 5 and CN 6, single-reference DFT converges to a ligand-reduced U(III) state inconsistent with formal $5f^3$ occupation, however the physical nature of this is still unresolved. Therefore, local coordination is a primary variable in the prediction of redox behavior in molten actinide-fluoride salts.

title: samQEq: universal charge equilibration for molecules and conductors
abstract: Charge equilibration assigns atomic charges by equalizing an atomic chemical potential built from electronegativity, hardness and the Coulomb interaction. Under one global constraint it lets charge flow without limit between molecules, which fluctuating-charge models prevent with one neutrality constraint per molecule. A metal needs the opposite: a global constraint and a hardness near zero, and there the charge operator becomes indefinite unless it includes each charge's own self-energy. Here, we present samQEq (solids-and-molecules QEq), a unified charge-equilibration package for LAMMPS that combines the two constructions in one energy functional and one matrix-free solve. An orthogonal projector imposes one neutrality constraint per molecule, and the finite-width self-energy of a Gaussian charge on designated conductor types, narrower than the conductor's own Gaussian, keeps the conductor's part of the operator positive definite at any hardness. On a gold slab carrying a water film, the operator stays definite down to the conductor limit of the model, the metal screens a point charge by a constant amount at every height beyond 4 Å, and the film's charges stay bounded under dynamics. Reciprocal-space electrostatics is evaluated inside the matrix-vector product, and three distinct shielding kernels are run-time settings. We verify the implementation by reproducing a published fluctuating-charge water model without refitting, and the native ReaxFF charge-equilibration step to approximately $10^{-9}\,e$. On a single four-V100 node the largest tested systems run at approximately twice the throughput of a 128-core CPU node. samQEq thus provides one charge-equilibration layer for molecules, conductors and the interfaces between them.

title: The nonexistence of nine-point crescent configurations
abstract: A planar crescent configuration consists of $n$ points, no three collinear and no four concyclic, whose distinct distances have multiplicities $1,2,\ldots,n-1$. We prove by exact computation that no such configuration exists for $n=9$. The three pairs carrying the two least frequent distances yield a six-point subset with at most six distances. Rational linear algebra on quartic polynomials separates the possible six-point distance patterns into those with certified finite lists of normalized distance tuples and a residual family. Compatibility of overlapping subsets forces at least one core into the first family, without classifying the residual realizations. The remaining three points are then obtained by rational constructions over the field of the squared core distances. The multiplication matrices used to enumerate the core distances have order at most twelve. Exhaustive label assignments and exact algebraic comparisons exclude all remaining extensions.

title: Cosmic Expansion in f(Q,C) Gravity: Observational Constraints and Geometric Diagnostics
abstract: We investigate the late-time expansion history of the Universe within the framework of $f(Q, C)$ gravity by adopting a linear parametrization of the deceleration parameter $q(z) = α+βH$, where $Q$ denotes the non-metricity scalar and $C$ represents the associated boundary term satisfying the geometrical relation $\mathring{R}= Q+C$. The adopted parametrization provides a phenomenological description of the cosmic expansion while retaining analytical tractability, allowing the transition from decelerated to accelerated expansion to be examined directly. An exact integration of the corresponding differential equation yields the closed-form Hubble function, $H(z)=\frac{1}{β\left[F_0-\ln(1+z)\right]},$ thereby providing an explicit description of the expansion history in terms of redshift. Here $F=\frac{1}β\sqrt{2βt+b}$ and $F_0$ specifies the value of $F$ at the present epoch. The model parameters are constrained using recent Cosmic Chronometer (CC) measurements, DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) observations, Pantheon+SH0ES Type Ia supernovae, and the Union3 observations through Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis. Individual and combined datasets are compared to assess the model's consistency, while its cosmic evolution is examined using the deceleration, the equation-of-state parameter, the state-finder pair ${r,s}$, and the $Om$ diagnostic.

title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control
abstract: Learned temporal models are moving beyond offline forecasting toward interactive environments for decision making, yet logged-trajectory accuracy need not predict closed-loop behavior under policies optimized in the learned model. This forecasting-control gap matters in tokamak magnetic control, where coupled plasma-circuit dynamics and actuator constraints can amplify errors through feedback. Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, we collect four datasets in a 2x2 design over physics-parameter and current-reference coverage. At matched budgets of 500, 1k, 3k, and 5k rollouts, we train 16 action-conditioned Transformers; PPO policies optimized in the 5k surrogates are then evaluated without adaptation on six reference-solver conditions. Only joint-coverage D4 shows monotonically decreasing cross-condition mean error, whereas D1 improves in distribution but degrades out of distribution. Binary completion masks substantial closed-loop differences: D2-D4 each complete 83.3% of conditions, but reach on average 99.0%, 94.7%, and 90.5% of the evaluation horizon, while their worst conditions reach 94.2%, 68.2%, and 43.2%. Policies trained with action noise complete 5/24 matched conditions, compared with 19/24 under nominal training, and have a lower mean horizon-capped episode length. Based on one trained policy per configuration and one evaluation realization per condition, the results support combining prediction error, episode completion, condition-level duration, and tracking quality.

title: Power Density as a Universal Biosignature: An Application to the Stellivore Hypothesis
abstract: Power density is a central measure underlying a common thread in cosmic evolution. It measures the rate at which free energy transits in a complex system of a given mass. We argue that it can be seen as a universal signature, and thus a strategy of ''following high power density'' can inform both biosignature and technosignature searches. We use known binary star masses and accretion rates to compute power densities of cataclysmic variables, neutron stars and transient black holes, and show that these accreting binaries have high power densities. We compare this result with other accreting systems in astrophysics as controls: young stellar objects (YSOs) and supermassive black holes (SMBHs). We review possible natural explanations, and then explore the possibility that these accreting binary systems might be instances of Type II stellar civilizations on Kardashev's scale, civilizations feeding on stars, or $\textit{stellivores}$. Besides power density, we present additional living clues, such as their variety, their existence far from thermodynamic equilibrium, their apparent homeostasis, the need to fine-tune models to explain them, the apparent existence of energy reserves, accretion control and ejection control, as well as other potential living systems functions. We summarize this case using living systems theory and discuss implications for big history.

title: Matter-Only Late-Time Acceleration via Barrow Entropy in Kaniadakis Statistics
abstract: The Barrow correction to the horizon entropy changes the total number of microstates associated with the horizon, whereas the Kaniadakis correction provides an alternate statistical description of these microstates different from Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics. In this paper, we consider the Kaniadakis description of the Barrow-corrected horizon entropy analogous to its description of the standard horizon entropy. The modified Friedmann equations were derived for an $(n+1)$-dimensional non-flat universe through two different approaches --- the law of emergence and the first law of thermodynamics. The generalised second law of thermodynamics was investigated, and the density contrast evolution equation was also derived. We take the universe to be composed of only matter and constrain the model parameters through an MCMC analysis using observational Hubble data, Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae data, baryon acoustic oscillation distances from the DESI DR2 data release, and $fσ_{8}$ measurements from redshift-space distortions. The Kaniadakis parameter $K$ was constrained away from zero, showing a preference for the $K$-deformed statistical approach. Motivated by recent studies, we considered a wider parameter space for the Barrow index, $Δ\in (-1,1]$. In agreement with observational data, we obtained $Δ= -0.335\pm0.031$, motivating a horizon structure different from Barrow's sphereflake configuration. The present value of the Hubble parameter was constrained as $H_{0}=(66.98 \pm 0.71)$ km/s/Mpc, which leans towards the early-universe Planck estimates; however, late-time data alone are insufficient to study the Hubble tension problem. Analysing the evolution of various cosmological parameters, we conclude that the modified Friedmann dynamics of the model produces a viable expansion history and late-time acceleration without invoking a dark energy component.

title: Hölder Duality and Self-Dual Arc Length on $L^p$ Unit Curves
abstract: We study arc length on the first-quadrant unit curve $x^p+y^p=1$, $p>1$, when length is measured with respect to an $L^r$ norm. Denoting this length by $L(p,r)$, we prove the Hölder-duality identity $L(p,r)=L(r^*,p^*)$, where $p^*=p/(p-1)$ and $r^*=r/(r-1)$. The identity is interpreted as a special case of the symmetry of mixed area (equivalently, of the anisotropic perimeter pairing). For the distinguished dual metric $r=p^*$, the length element agrees with the areal angular element: $L(p,p^*)=\int_γ(x\,dy-y\,dx)=\frac1p B(1/p,1/p)$. Thus the familiar coincidence between arc length and angular parameter on the Euclidean unit circle is the self-dual case $p=2$ of a more general relation between $L^p$ geometry and its dual metric. As a consequence, the Euclidean arc length of the $L^p$ unit curve admits a dual trigonometric representation.

title: Birefringence in non-linear electrodynamics emerging from a Lorentz-symmetry violation scenario
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classical properties of a non-linear electrodynamics that emerges from one loop effective action for fermions coupled to an antisymmetric background tensor, that breaks the Lorentz symmetry in the model. The conservation laws are obtained through the Belinfante-Rosenfeld energy-momentum tensor in the non-linear electrodynamics that provides the energy density, the Poynting vector, the linear momentum and the stress tensor. In particular, this Lorentz symmetry violation breaks the symmetric index of the energy-momentum tensor, but it preserves the gauge invariance, as we expect. We introduce the prescription of a magnetic background field, that we consider constant and uniform. For propagation effects, the model is linearized by the magnetic background. This prescription allows us investigations of the plane wave propagation in the presence of an external magnetic field. In this context, we obtain the constitutive relations of the material medium, that behaves like an bi-anisotropic medium. Thereby, we calculate the refractive index whose one of the solutions show the total absorption of the wave in the medium. Using the wave equation for linear polarization, we investigate the birefringence phenomenon when the linear wave polarization changes with the magnetic background direction. The birefringence is so related to one of the spatial component of the LSV tensor in which we estimate through the PVLS experiment. We use one of the dispersion relations to obtain the kinematic of the Compton effect in the presence of the LSV parameter.

title: On Gallai $d$-colored circulants
abstract: A $d$-graph is a complete graph whose edges are colored with colors from $[d]$. It is Gallai if it contains no triangle whose three edges have distinct colors. We prove that every Gallai $d$-circulant is an iterated lexicographic product of circulants using at most two colors. The proof uses the compatibility of the known canonical modular decomposition with the cyclic action. For $d$-graphs avoiding both a rainbow triangle $Δ$ and the two-colored four-vertex graph $Π$ whose chromatic components are paths, we give a more explicit classification. Color-preserving vertex transitivity is equivalent to circular symmetry and to a reduced positional game tree whose branching numbers and labels depend only on depth. The edge colors in the given cyclic labeling are determined by a chain of divisors of the order. This description yields a complete isomorphism invariant and a linear-time recognition procedure in the difference-word representation. The characterization of CIS $d$-circulants reduces to CIS two-colored factors. Finally, we extend the numerical CIS criterion to $d$-graphs whose chromatic components are vertex-transitive.

title: Steerable Single-step Retrosynthesis with Electron-pushing Discrete Flow Matching and Feynman-Kac Steering
abstract: Expert chemists perform retrosynthetic analysis in a strategic manner, where each reaction in a route is employed with a specific purpose, combined with mechanistic reasoning represented as electron-pushing arrows to visualize how bonds are formed or broken via electron redistribution. Yet contemporary single-step retrosynthesis models exhibit neither of these properties: their learned reaction distribution is fixed to that of the training data, and reactions are predicted via de-novo generation of the precursors or molecular graph edits, omitting the electron redistribution that governs the chemical transformations. We introduce Verso MAELLE, the first electron-pushing-based single-step retrosynthetic model, representing disconnections as continuous-time Markov chains (CTMC) comprised of edits in the electron space, and is trainable using a discrete flow matching formulation. Being a generative model, Verso MAELLE is optionally steerable at inference time through the Feynman-Kac (FK) framework, using rewards that promote certain types of disconnections. We show that besides in-distribution learning, Verso MAELLE can be steered toward cyclization reactions which are scaffold-constructive but underrepresented in the training corpus, via a ring-breaking reward. As a proof of concept, we show how the electron-pushing reasoning, learned from patented data, combined with a domino incentivizing reward, could steer Verso MAELLE toward creative and strategic disconnections, demonstrated on the key domino sequence that was used to synthesize Punctaporonin U, a complex natural product of the sesquiterpene family.

title: The Umami Chaplygin Gas as a Unified Dark Fluid: Observational Constraints, Perturbative and Thermodynamic Stability Analysis
abstract: We study a cosmological scenario in which the Universe contains standard baryonic matter, radiation, and a single unified dark fluid, the umami Chaplygin gas, which accounts for both dark matter and dark energy with no separate dark-matter component. We first analyse the thermodynamic behaviour of the fluid and show that, unlike earlier Chaplygin-type models, its thermodynamic stability is conditional rather than global: stability holds only above a critical density $ρ_1=\sqrt{|A/w|}$, the fluid reheats once this density is crossed, and a viable low-density regime requires $|w|<2$. Thermodynamic stability at the present epoch requires $|A|<|w|ρ_0^2$, a condition that is more easily met for $|w|>1$. We then constrain both the $|w|<1$ and $|w|>1$ cases with Type Ia supernovae, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, cosmic-chronometer Hubble data and Planck 2018 distance priors through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis. The $|w|<1$ case fits all four datasets well, with $w \simeq -0.73$, $Ω_m^{\rm eff} \simeq 0.32$ and $H_0 \simeq 66.8$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. It is statistically comparable to flat $Λ$CDM, with $Δ{\rm AIC}=-4.8$ and $Δ{\rm BIC}=+0.6$. Its best-fit parameters violate the stability condition. The $|w|>1$ case with a Gaussian prior satisfies the condition but fits worse, with $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq+66$ relative to $Λ$CDM. The best fit that obeys the condition exactly still has $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq+50$. Finally, a linear perturbation analysis shows that the adiabatic sound speed turns negative at exactly the same critical density, triggering exponential small-scale growth at late times in the observationally preferred case. These results reveal a tension between a good fit to background data and the physical stability of the umami unified dark fluid.

title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) aims to enable AI systems to autonomously build and improve AI systems themselves, including models, harnesses, and underlying infrastructure. Within this broader agenda, a central capability is enabling agents to train and improve base models. However, existing studies on automated model training primarily focused on workflow- or harness-level optimizations, rather than internalizing the ability to conduct post-training into the model itself. Developing this capability requires executable model training environments that can produce high-quality trajectories demonstrating how to select data, train models, diagnose failures, and iteratively improve results. In this paper, we introduce RSI-Dojo, a collection of executable model training environments designed to teach LLM agents to conduct post-training. To construct RSI-Dojo, we develop RSI-Craft, an automatic pipeline that converts human research artifacts into executable model training environments. RSI-Craft automatically collects research papers from top venues, instantiates datasets and metrics into a unified interface, and reproduces evaluation dependencies. It then filters tasks by data size, execution reliability, and discriminability, yielding RSI-Dojo with 281 seed model training tasks. Building on RSI-Dojo, we employ a trajectory collection method with an improved harness to collect high-quality model-training trajectories from frontier models, then retain examples through rubric-based and outcome-based filtering. We fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories. The resulting RSI-Dojo-9B and RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B improve over their base models by 8.74 and 16.87 PostTrainBench points, respectively. RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B reaches 29.95 on PostTrainBench and 53.29 on PostTrainBench-Lite, matching the performance of frontier models such as GLM-5.2 and GPT 5.5.

title: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search
abstract: Locating competing reaction pathways is difficult when potential-energy gradients are unavailable. Here we present tReax\_expedition, an energy-only approach combining coupled Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labelling and restrained continuation. Exploration identifies connected states, while continuation resolves candidate channels and records sampled chain maxima. Single-search benchmarks on three two-dimensional potentials recovered an intermediate and competing routes without transition-state guesses. For eight of nine gas-phase reactions on GFN2-xTB, sampled chain maxima differed from independently refined saddle energies by less than 0.76~kJ\,mol$^{-1}$. Alanine dipeptide instead revealed incomplete conformational relaxation, showing that route connectivity can persist despite structural and energetic errors. Neural committor learning and local straddling-pair sampling connect the resulting paths to transition-region sampling, although molecular shooting diagnostics indicate limited committor calibration. These results show how energy-only exploration and continuation recover candidate pathways, while distinguishing route connectivity from geometric localization, barrier resolution and finite-temperature transition statistics.

title: Constructions of Variable Modified Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel Gases from Geometrothermodynamics
abstract: Understanding the physical origin of the Universe's late-time accelerated expansion remains one of the central open problems in modern cosmology. Geometrothermodynamics (GTD) offers a compelling route to this problem, providing a geometric framework that unifies thermodynamics with contact and Riemannian geometry to encode the equilibrium properties of a physical system directly into its underlying geometric structure. In this work, we employ the GTD formalism to investigate cosmological models capable of explaining the observed accelerated expansion of the Universe. As an important outcome, our simple model exhibits dynamical behavior that provides a reasonable description of the late-time evolution of the Universe. We study the Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel gas models and their variable forms within geometrothermodynamics by deriving their thermodynamic relations, entropy, and equations of state. The free parameters of the models are constrained through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using several observational datasets, including cosmic chronometers combined with baryon acoustic oscillations (CC+BAO), DESI DR2 BAO data, DESI DR2 combined with the DES-SN5YR and Union3 Type Ia supernova compilations. The statistical performance of the models is assessed using the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria (AIC and BIC). We further examine their cosmological evolution through the deceleration parameter, the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, and higher-order kinematic diagnostics, including the jerk and snap parameters. The perturbative stability of the models is also investigated through the squared sound speed.

title: Naturalization of Vinti's intermediary orbit---or how to get rid of small divisors in Brouwer's satellite solution
abstract: A naturalization, in the sense of Deprit, of Vinti's dynamical system makes the construction of a first order analytical satellite perturbation solution without critical divisors possible. The process gives hints on how to recast Brouwer's classical solution in a form that is free from small divisors too. The functionality of classical perturbation solutions is in this way extended to the close vicinity of the critical inclination. The new analytical solution bears terms that may grow unbounded, but their negative effects do not disclose in time intervals in which this kind of solution may be useful in practice.

title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
abstract: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

title: SecRed: A program for sector-wise IBP reduction of Feynman integrals
abstract: SecRed is a C++ program for the reduction of multi-loop Feynman integrals with integration-by-parts (IBP) identities. It reduces an integral family sector by sector for memory control and parallelism, and adds algorithms designed for that setting: an adaptive seed box with a corner cut, an optional seed truncation, a subsector level filter, and symmetry relations expanded only from the master integrals of a sector. A global stage assembles the retained equations and performs the finite-field reconstruction of the coefficients using FiniteFlow or FireFly, repeating the elimination over a sequence of primes. On the elimination side, a coefficient-free plan records the elimination order once and is replayed at each prime, so that only the arithmetic is repeated, and a head score orders the equations to reduce fill-in during the elimination. The program is demonstrated on a two-loop five-point non-planar family and on a four-loop cut family, where assembling the global equation system as a whole would exceed the memory of a single node.

title: Fine structure of fermion mixing and quark-mass hierarchies
abstract: We investigate a semi-empirical flavour framework based on two linked hypotheses: a golden/pentagonal organisation of fermion mixing and the recurrence of its hierarchy maps in the quark-mass spectrum. The two large lepton angles are specified by the fifth-order Chebyshev conditions $T_5(θ_{12}^{\ell})=0$ and $T_5(θ_{23}^{\ell})=-1$, with angular arguments in radian measure, while the smaller reactor angle follows the approximate bilinear relation $θ_{13}^{\ell}\simeqθ_{12}^{\ell}θ_{23}^{\ell}/π$. An alternative golden-partition construction yields nearly identical large-angle predictions and an exact circular--hyperbolic duality. The golden ratio $φ$ also enters two distinct geometrical prescriptions for the Cabibbo angle, while the heptadecagonal seed $α_C=π/17$ governs the suppressed mixing hierarchy. The near-equality $\tanα_C\simeq\cos54^\circ/π$ further connects the two geometries. The resulting quark hierarchy obeys the quadratic map $θ_{13}^q=\sqrt{θ_C^2+(θ_{23}^q)^2}-θ_C\simeq(θ_{23}^q)^2/(2θ_C)$. Transferring the quadratic and bilinear maps to quark masses yields the crossed relations $m_d\simeq m_c^2/(2m_t)$ and $m_u\simeq m_b m_s/(m_F/φ)$, where $m_F=G_F^{-1/2}$. The complementary triples $(t,c,d)$ and $(b,s,u)$ reproduce both mass targets within $1\%$ for the adopted reference values. Gatto--Sartori--Tonin-type correspondences and Froggatt--Nielsen scaling provide compatible phenomenological interpretations. These results suggest a common golden/geometrical organising structure for flavour mixing and mass hierarchies, whose underlying dynamical origin remains to be established.

title: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to assist spreadsheet users with tasks such as spreadsheet model construction, formula generation, and data analysis, yet their interaction with real-world spreadsheets remains limited by the mismatch between the structure of spreadsheets and the sequential textual representations typically provided to LLMs. We propose a compact formula-aware spreadsheet abstraction that represents large homogeneous ranges through their positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and selected boundary values. An efficient algorithm detects and structures these ranges before a textual serialization is supplied to an LLM. The abstraction is provided to the LLM before detailed spreadsheet content is submitted, improving the accuracy and efficiency of spreadsheet processing while reducing token consumption. We evaluate the method on 50 spreadsheet-query cases. The evaluation shows that the abstraction alone was sufficient to answer some queries. When additional spreadsheet content is required, the abstraction reduces the amount of data that must be submitted to the LLM, thereby reducing token consumption. The abstraction layer also improves the reliability and accuracy of spreadsheet processing. We conclude by discussing further techniques for combining spreadsheet static analysis with artificial intelligence to improve the reliability, accuracy, and efficiency of AI assisted spreadsheet tasks.

title: Quantum banking system for secure cash withdrawal
abstract: A quantum-secure withdrawal framework is presented by replacing reproducible classical credentials with quantum tokens for authentication. The protocol integrates token generation, authentication, and verification into the existing banking workflow using experimentally motivated quantum control techniques. This mitigates card cloning, credential theft, and counterfeiting.

title: Surface chemistry as data for level-set simulation of etching and deposition
abstract: Level-set simulators of etching and deposition move the surface with a velocity that depends on adsorbate coverages. These coverages are usually computed from balances solved and coded by hand for each chemistry, whereas voxel-based Monte Carlo profile simulators read the reaction mechanism as data. For the open-source level-set simulator ViennaPS, this work presents a surface model whose rate laws, Jacobian and velocity are derived from a reaction file and evaluated with ray-traced fluxes. Steady-state coverages are obtained with Newton's method and transient coverages with a conservative integrator. One compiled model is applied to eight chemistries for chemical vapour deposition, selective epitaxy, plasma etching, sputtering and atomic layer deposition. It reproduces a hand-written silicon etch model to seven significant digits at a single point and within the Monte Carlo noise in a masked trench. In a high-aspect-ratio cavity, alumina conformality is determined by a trimethylaluminium reaction probability within the measured range.

title: Nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild black holes for the Einstein-massless Dirac system in spherical symmetry
abstract: In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild exterior for the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless Dirac system. More precisely, we consider sufficiently small perturbations of Schwarzschild characteristic initial data and prove that the corresponding maximal development remains globally controlled in the exterior region (orbital stability), and converges, in a suitable teleological double-null gauge, to a Schwarzschild spacetime with a final mass (asymptotic stability). In particular, the maximal future development contains a complete future null infinity and a regular event horizon, with a nonempty black hole region in its interior. The main difficulties in the proof arise from the delicate coupling between the Dirac operator and the geometry, compared with the scalar wave counterpart, as well as from the failure of the Dirac stress-energy tensor to satisfy a positive energy condition. To overcome these difficulties, we rely on a bootstrap argument coupling the geometry and the Dirac field. Working in suitable teleological double-null gauges adapted to the asymptotic null boundaries, we establish weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the event horizon, and an rp-estimates towards null infinity. A core ingredient is the use of suitable reweightings of the spinor components, which allow us to close these estimates despite the nonlinear coupling to the geometry.

title: InterceptFuzz: Interception-based Stateful Fuzzing of Single-Process Targets
abstract: Stateful protocol implementations are commonly fuzzed by tools that act as a network client and exchange messages with the target over sockets. Some wireless and IoT protocol stacks instead provide a single-process simulation platform, in which all nodes run in one binary and exchange packets in memory. Such simulations are deterministic and fast, which suits fuzzing, but offer no socket to which existing stateful fuzzers can attach. Meanwhile, fuzzing infrastructure such as Google's OSS-Fuzz supports only stateless engines. This paper presents InterceptFuzz, a middleware that enables stateful fuzzing of single-process targets on top of an unmodified stateless fuzzing engine. InterceptFuzz requires only a hook where the target passes packets between nodes. Through this hook, it records benign traffic and injects fuzzed packets. It organizes the observed packet sequences in a Prefix Tree. Each seed carries a State ID that selects a node of this tree, and InterceptFuzz deterministically replays the recorded prefix before delivering the mutated packet. The tree grows with newly discovered sequences, while redundant states are pruned to keep its growth in check. InterceptFuzz powered by AFL++ is evaluated on the Nexus test framework of OpenThread and on the LTE and Wi-Fi models of ns-3, against an interception-based adaptation of AFLNet and against Concat, an AFL++-based baseline that mutates a whole message sequence as one input. On OpenThread and ns-3 Wi-Fi, InterceptFuzz covers significantly more branches than both baselines. Seven previously unknown crash signatures were found in OpenThread. Concat, despite its simplicity, covers more branches than AFLNet in every campaign on OpenThread and ns-3 Wi-Fi, and on OpenThread it exposes the same crash signatures as InterceptFuzz, although some of them in fewer campaigns.

title: te-comp: A Complete MLIR Compiler Generating Self-Contained C Inference Engines for MCUs
abstract: Deploying deep learning on microcontrollers (MCUs) requires fitting both the model weights and runtime activations within tens to hundreds of kilobytes of SRAM and Flash. Existing approaches either use an interpreter with a pre-written kernel library or combine a Python code generator with hand-written C kernels. This incurs dispatch overhead and requires framework dependencies. None produces self-contained, dependency-free C code specialized to a given model. In this paper, we present te-comp, the first complete MLIR-based compiler that takes a standard model in .tflite or .safetensors format and emits all C source files needed for deployment: the inference engine (kernels, weight arrays, memory layout) and the RTOS integration layer with zero runtime dependencies. On 10 MCUNet CNN benchmarks, te-comp outperforms MCUNet TinyEngine by using 38% less SRAM (up to 5.9$\times$) and 15% less Flash, while generating complete C code rather than linking a pre-written kernel library. To demonstrate, we use te-comp to compile an 8.3M-parameter GPT-Neo transformer (TinyStories-v2) and deploy it on a single-core Cortex-M7 at 160MHz. The full firmware uses 249KB of 512KB SRAM and 3.62MB of 4MB Flash and achieves approximately 1 token/s interactive text generation via Q4_0 weight quantization, a stateful int4 KV cache, and vocabulary pruning -- a capability no existing MCU inference framework supports.

title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

title: Native transverse-momentum evolution and matching for TMD factorization and extraction
abstract: We present a native transverse-momentum realization of the Collins/CSS2 leading-power transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization framework. The construction connects fixed-order distributional matching, origin contacts, unexpanded two-scale evolution, and a differentiable interface for hadronic structure. An endpoint-independent canonical scale with a specified infrared completion generates a Collins--Soper kernel on a common invariant domain. Complete canonical legs are bounded and admit constructive momentum-space evaluation through resolvent convolutions or elliptic solves. We give contact and finite-bin error bounds, parent-to-momentum-boundary translations, ordered flavor recurrences, and an all-order argument for the four exponent towers of $N^3\mathrm{LL}$ evolution. Localized joint-$(x,k_T)$ inputs, nonperturbative rapidity broadening, regulated moments and the full-spectrum subtraction are formulated as distinct parts of the prescription. The physical realization uses sourced four-loop beta/cusp and three-loop noncusp/Collins--Soper ingredients with strict-NLO hard/OPE boundaries. Non-Gaussian continuum tests and three-scale physical-PDF comparisons validate ordinary legs, contacts, individual insertions and analytic input derivatives. Including a declared bound on the continuation above a finite PDF table, physical bin discrepancies remain below $4.27\times10^{-5}$ of the peak reference bin. A qualified proton--proton Drell--Yan and neural-closure demonstration connects the method to inverse use. Higher-order boundary assembly and matched observables are specified without claiming an implemented $N^3\mathrm{LL}'$ spectrum or a completed global extraction.

title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language: ordinary, delay, or partial differential equations, discrete maps, static and causal models, or stochastic processes, possibly with hidden states, distorted sensors, and uninformative measurement channels. The agent buys experiments within a budget, writes candidate programs in the same language, obtains their coefficients from the benchmark's fitter, and is scored only on how its final program predicts experiments it never saw: conditions outside the range it could explore, interventions, and longer runs. Across 80 systems in 20 domains, nine language models solve between 21% and 60%. On 44 of these systems, classical equation-discovery methods almost never succeed, although the same data usually suffice once the true equations are given with unknown coefficients; the difficulty lies in finding the structure, not in estimating it. Because mechanisms recur across systems, we also give agents the program they discovered for a related system; it helped only when the new system shared the mechanism and the first investigation had succeeded. Stronger agents make fewer unscientific errors; beyond these, agents find which variables a system has but not how they act, and prefer revisions that lower the training error to revisions that predict better.

title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.

title: Equational theories of min-plus semirings
abstract: We study the equational theory and subvarieties of the variety $\mathcal V$ generated by $(\mathbb N_0,\min,+)$. We prove that a subvariety of $\mathcal V$ is proper if and only if it is locally finite, equivalently, if and only if it satisfies a power-stabilization identity. Every finite member generates a hereditarily finitely based variety with a finite subvariety lattice. In contrast, the periodic subvarieties defined by $x^m=x^{m+1}$ are nonfinitely based for $m\geq2$. We construct a strictly descending chain of nonfinitely based subvarieties and three varieties generated by explicit reduced products, each with a decidable equational theory. The smallest is a limit variety: it is nonfinitely based, and every proper subvariety has an absolute finite identity basis. The subvariety lattice of $\mathcal V$ has cardinality continuum. In fact, the interval between the first reduced-product variety and the subvariety defined by $x^2=x^3$ already has this cardinality, and all its members are nonfinitely based. We also give a hereditarily finitely based example with an infinite subvariety lattice. The constructions use finite convex models and recognition quotients.

title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
abstract: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.

title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) and incorporates PDE constraints through finite-difference residuals evaluated at off-sensor collocation points. These residuals provide additional physical information in regions without direct observational supervision. PhysFTM first reconstructs continuous spatial fields at support frames via an alternating minimization scheme, optimizing the Tucker core tensor and the RKHS-based factors separately. To enable missing-frame reconstruction, PhysFTM constructs a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space, which is decoded by the learned spatial RKHS-FTM representation to recover the full spatiotemporal field. Experiments on Allen--Cahn, Navier--Stokes, three-dimensional Heat equations, and a three-dimensional gridded Copernicus ocean reanalysis demonstrate accurate 2D/3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/liusirzzz/PhysFTM.

title: NepTTS-Bench: Native-Speaker Benchmarking and NepaliMOS for Nepali Text-to-Speech
abstract: Nepali TTS has reached a point where multiple systems are available, but there is no shared evaluation to compare them. NepTTS-Bench was created to address what existing automated and manual evaluation systems lack for Nepali TTS. A controlled benchmark with phonological grounding which contains 205 sentences (77 minimal pairs targeting aspiration, retroflex/dental contrasts, nasalization, gemination, and schwa deletion) which is rated by 180 speakers. There are 6,962 ratings for 10 TTS configurations and two human references. Along with this 7 ASR systems were evaluated for round-trip CER. SCOREQ was also run as an automated baseline. The key finding is that automated evaluation like SCOREQ prefers proprietary systems like ElevenLabs but native listeners prefer Piper. This is contributed by the fact that most of the systems not properly tuned for Nepali tend to show Hindi phonological behaviour and our minimal pairs are designed to surface such contrasts. We also present NepaliMOS predictor which is fine tuned on collected ratings. NepaliMOS achieves system-level rho = 0.90 on the dense panel but drops to utterance-level rho = 0.43 under leave-one-system-out evaluation. This is statistically significant and confirms that NepaliMOS captures genuine signal but cross-provider transfer is limited. A human calibration is recommended for new systems for which we release a Python evaluation package for practitioners to run the benchmark against new systems.

title: How Does One Cut a 30-60-90 Triangle?
abstract: We enumerate dissections of a 30-60-90 triangle into smaller triangles similar to itself, counting unlabeled arrangements up to similarity and reflection. There are 18 four-piece, 121 five-piece, and 844 six-piece arrangements, corresponding to 11, 47, and 235 distinct multisets of piece areas. We present illustrated catalogs organized by these area multisets and distinguish layouts obtained by subdivision and local rotations or reflections from independent layouts. A separately implemented computational search reproduces every arrangement up to nine pieces, finding 460404 arrangements. Counts through nine pieces for five other classes of triangles are included for comparison.

title: Stabilization of kinetic plasma instabilities via instantaneous external field control
abstract: We propose an instantaneous control framework for the stabilization of kinetic plasma instabilities using external fields. The control problem is formulated as a PDE-constrained optimization that accounts for nonlinear plasma dynamics, while the control is determined at each time step to avoid global-in-time optimization. The Discretize-then-Optimize (DtO) approach is adopted, with the forward equations first discretized using a particle-in-cell (PIC) method. The subsequent control computation is derived from the discrete particle update, ensuring consistency with the forward solver. The control objective is formulated in terms of electromagnetic field energy and low-order moments rather than the full distribution function, making the optimization more amenable to practical implementation. The framework is applied to both electrostatic and electromagnetic settings and evaluated on several benchmark problems, including the two-stream, bump-on-tail, Dory--Guest--Harris, and Weibel instabilities. Across these tests, the control successfully suppresses field energy growth and keeps the distribution function close to its initial state. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in suppressing kinetic plasma instabilities.

title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair; second, because physical theories must interact with the real world, it uses computational physics as an executable testbed while separating the qualification of numerical instruments from scientific claim review so solvers and diagnostics can be adapted within a recorded investigation. We apply the framework in an 82.6 h investigation to tackle the long-standing problem of radiated energy exceeding the imploding-shell kinetic energy in a Z-pinch. The investigation reveals competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing. Stronger coherent helical deformation increases resistive conversion while reducing radiation and increasing retained energy. A broader trailing-plasma profile delays the later radiation maximum and recovers much of its early bolometric deficit, with a spectral response that changes during the pulse. These results provide new insight into energy conversion in high-energy-density plasma physics and demonstrate a new paradigm for physics research.

title: A Neuroprosthetic SoC Featuring Rapid Local Sensory Feedback with On-Chip Unsupervised Multi-Class Spike Sorting
abstract: This letter presents a 65 nm neuroprosthetic system-on-chip (SoC) featuring a rapid feedback pathway from motor recording to sensory stimulation. To enable low-latency sensory mapping modulated by individual-neuron firing rates, the SoC integrates a mixed-signal unsupervised spike-sorting module with stimulation-artifact rejection, a programmable sliding-window firing-rate calculator, and a closed-loop controller for adapting stimulation parameters. The spike-sorting module combines event-driven analog feature extraction with Manhattan-distance-based digital clustering while consuming 1.6 $μ$W/channel. On the Quiroga Difficult-1 benchmark, it achieves 94.58% three-class accuracy, with only a 0.4% reduction when stimulation artifacts are introduced at 20% of the spike count. The closed-loop controller supports polynomial and logarithmic mapping functions and incorporates Mitchell's approximation for power saving. The SoC is fully characterized on the bench and in vivo.

title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
abstract: Deep Research (DR) systems extend large language models into autonomous agents that decompose complex information needs, iteratively search the web, and synthesize evidence to answer challenging questions. However, their multi-stage execution may introduce robustness risks, as variations in user questions or intermediate search inputs may propagate across research stages and lead to incorrect answers. Existing evaluations focus on task-solving capabilities or robustness against external evidence disturbances, leaving intrinsic weaknesses in DR execution insufficiently explored. Thus, we conduct an empirical study of 1,932 execution trajectories from three representative DR systems and identify nine recurring defect categories across subquestion formulation, online search, and final reasoning. Guided by these findings, we propose EMBERS, an empirically motivated, defect-guided fuzzing framework for robustness testing of DR systems. Starting from correctly answered seed questions, EMBERS generates stage-targeted test inputs using defect-guided mutation, web-search-assisted fidelity assurance, and diversity-aware seed maintenance. Experiments across 16 framework--model--dataset settings show that EMBERS achieves 3.21 times the failure-discovery throughput of the strongest baseline under identical testing budgets.
